items.title: libct: fail if additional gids cannot be set
items.body:
When `setgroups(2)` is denied in the container user namespace (e.g. when runc
is run inside `unshare -r`, or the container joins such a user namespace), runc
silently skipped setting the supplementary groups, so a container (or exec)
explicitly configured with additional gids started successfully without them.

Return an error instead. An additional gid equal to the process gid is
tolerated, since it is in effect anyway; this is what Podman passes when running
with a single ID mapping (it always adds the user's primary gid), so that setup
keeps working.

The rootless EUID case is already rejected earlier, in `(*Container).start`.

The new integration test creates an external user namespace with setgroups
denied, joins it, and checks both `runc run` and `runc exec`. It is written to
also pass with crun (with containers/crun#2321).

Originally reported for crun in containers/crun#2320; crun counterpart is
containers/crun#2321.

items.body:
Found by the cloud round-4 review (R4-F1) of `fix/6118-promo6-ssh` at 323d27aec and re-verified open at `cef00dba9` by the round-5 security review (reviewer ai:f1-secrev-6118).

## Root cause
The prune-script tests that make an entry unreadable/unremovable with `chmod` (`scripts/test/test_ci_runner_target_hygiene_6118.py`, the `chmod(0)` / `chmod(0o500)` sites around lines 1560, 1640, 1680) assume mode bits deny access. Under uid 0, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE ignores mode bits, so the expected EACCES never happens. There is no uid-0 skip (the only skip is the APFS non-UTF-8 one at line 1841).

## Impact
Defect class: test-environment fragility. The suite (and Section G of the CI invariants gate that runs it) goes red in any root container although the script is correct.

## Evidence (executed)
On f2, tree from `git archive cef00dba9`: as uid 1000 `Ran 85 tests ... OK`; under `unshare -r` (uid 0) `Ran 85 tests ... FAILED (failures=3, errors=2)`: `test_6118_unremovable_entry_warns_continues_and_exits_1`, `test_6118_scan_unreadable_subdir_warns_and_prunes_the_rest`, `test_6118_newline_in_entry_name_cannot_inject_a_workflow_command`.

## Repro
`unshare -r python3 -m unittest scripts.test.test_ci_runner_target_hygiene_6118` on Linux.

## Proposed fix
`scripts/test/test_ci_runner_target_hygiene_6118.py` (~8 lines): a module constant `UID0 = hasattr(os, "geteuid") and os.geteuid() == 0` and `if UID0: self.skipTest("uid 0 ignores mode bits (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE)")` at the top of the three tests, mirroring the APFS skip; or, better for coverage, have those tests inject the OSError by replacing `os.unlink`/`os.scandir` in-process when UID0 (~20 lines).

items.body:
## Problem

`src/lib/conversions/media-ffprobe.ts` runs `ffprobe` on uploaded media without the namespace sandbox, even when `STRICT_SANDBOX` is on. A hostile file reaches a native parser with network access and the worker's PID view.

## Proposal

- Run ffprobe through `resolveSandboxedCommand` / `executeSandboxedBinary` with `networkIsolated: true` and the same rlimits as the ffmpeg path.
- Let `SandboxUnavailableError` propagate (503).

## Acceptance criteria

- A spy-binary test proves ffprobe is started under `unshare -r -n` in strict mode.
- With the sandbox unavailable, a media conversion answers 503 and ffprobe is never spawned.

items.title: command: move socket to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
items.body:
(Cleanup) This moves the py3-cmd socket out of the shared `/tmp`, into the user's runtime directory.

----
The socket was `/tmp/py3status_uds.<pid>`, in the `/tmp` all users share, and `py3-cmd` tried every user's sockets there. The runtime directory is private to the user, and it's where programs keep their sockets.

- command: put the socket in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or `/run/user/<uid>` when it isn't set (eg `py3-cmd` from cron), so py3status and `py3-cmd` find the same place; `/tmp` only when there is neither.
- command: name it `py3status.<pid>.sock` instead of `py3status_uds.<pid>`.
- command: `py3-cmd` run as root also looks in every user's runtime directory, so a pacman hook (Arch ships `py3status-refresh-arch_updates.hook`) still reaches their bars, as it did through `/tmp`.

After upgrading, restart py3status: a `py3-cmd` from this version looks only in the runtime directory, not in `/tmp`.

Tested: `pytest tests`: 246 passed. py3status run with a test config: the socket is `/run/user/1000/py3status.<pid>.sock` and is removed on exit, and `py3-cmd refresh` reaches it normally and with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset. The pacman hook's command, `py3-cmd refresh arch_updates`, run as root (uid 0 through `unshare -r`, with an empty environment like pacman's) refreshes the bar's `arch_updates`.

items.title: Let CI run the egress sandbox's Linux layer 2
items.body:
The egress allowlist (#22, PR #91) has two layers on Linux: an allowlist proxy, and unprivileged user, network and mount namespaces (`unshare -r -n -m`) so a process that ignores proxy variables still cannot leave. On `ubuntu-latest` the namespace layer is unavailable to an unprivileged process: `detect_layer_two()` returns `none`, the layer-2 unit test (`tests/unit/egress/test_sandbox.py::test_a_wrapped_process_reaches_only_the_allowlist`) skips, and L0-17 passes on its proxy-denial path. CI run 39916580533 shows 11 skipped against 10 on a macOS host, which is that one test.

The likely cause is Ubuntu 24.04's `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`. One step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, before the tests, should enable the full test:

```yaml
- name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (egress layer 2)
  run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
```

The workflow is the maintainers' file, so this is an issue rather than a PR. If the step is added and the test still skips, the job log's "skipped" count and `uv run python -c "from vlah.adapters.executor.sandbox.sandbox import detect_layer_two; print(detect_layer_two())"` say why. The same tests pass in an Ubuntu 24.04 container with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined --security-opt apparmor=unconfined`.

items.title: deep-review: n7-honeypot-detect — TST: test_scan_range_no_root_refuses fails whenever the suite runs as root (i.e. in the CI you are about to add)
items.body:
## Severity: High

`tests/test_honeypot_detect.py:74-83` asserts the root gate refuses. The gate is
`os.geteuid() == 0`, so the test **only passes in a non-root environment** and fails in
root — which is the default for container-based CI, Docker, and `sudo -u` root runners.

### Where

- `tests/test_honeypot_detect.py:74-83` — `TestGatekeeping.test_scan_range_no_root_refuses`
  asserts `assertNotEqual(r.returncode, 0)`
- `firmware/honeypot_detect.py:455-458` — `if not os.geteuid() == 0 and (args.scan_range or args.live): sys.exit(1)`
- `firmware/honeypot_detect.py:452-453` — as root the gate is passed and the scan proceeds

### Reproduction (verified)

Non-root (the maintainer's shell):

```
$ python3 -m pytest -q
11 passed in 3.20s
```

Same tree, same interpreter, running as uid 0 (`unshare -r`, i.e. a user namespace that
maps to root — equivalent to `docker run` / a root CI runner):

```
$ unshare -r python3 -m pytest -q
.........F.                                                              [100%]
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
_______________ TestGatekeeping.test_scan_range_no_root_refuses ________________
>       self.assertNotEqual(r.returncode, 0)
E       AssertionError: 0 == 0
tests/test_honeypot_detect.py:82: AssertionError
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/test_honeypot_detect.py::TestGatekeeping::test_scan_range_no_root_refuses
1 failed, 10 passed in 3.21s
```

The test *passes the gate* and then **really scans `127.0.0.1-10`** with the default
18-port list, because the assertion it makes depends on the ambient privilege level.

### Why this blocks the obvious next step

Issue #1 recommends adding a CI workflow. The moment that workflow uses
`container:`/`runs-on` with a root user — the standard setup for a Python security tool —
this test fails the build. The failure is unrelated to the code under test, so it would be
diagnosed as "flaky test" and either re-run away or disabled.

### Safe remediation (lowest-risk first)

1. **Best:** extract the gate so it is testable without ambient privilege, e.g.
   ```python
   def _live_allowed(args, euid=None):
       return (euid if euid is not None else os.geteuid()) == 0
   ```
   then unit-test it with explicit `euid=0` and `euid=1000` values, plus keep one
   subprocess test that only asserts the *message* (`'--harness' in stdout`) rather than
   the exit code. No behaviour change for real users.
2. If the gate must stay inline, mark the test explicitly privileged and run the
   subprocess with the privilege dropped, e.g. `subprocess.run(..., user=...)` (Python 3.9+)
   or a preexec_fn that calls `os.setuid`. Assert the exit code there.
3. Lowest-effort fallback if neither is wanted: `@unittest.skipIf(os.geteuid() == 0, ...)`
   — correct, but note it silently drops the only gate coverage in root CI, so prefer 1.
4. Independently, add `os.name == 'nt'` handling: `os.geteuid()` does not exist on
   Windows, so `main()` raises `AttributeError` there. Use
   `getattr(os, 'geteuid', lambda: 1)()`.

### Note

`README.md:73` claims `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — **11 unit tests (exit 0)**.
That is accurate for a non-root run and is the command a new CI job will use.

items.title: FileTrust: the delegation clause never meets a real root-owned file on an unprivileged host, and a user namespace can construct one

labels.name: type/test
labels.description: Coverage gaps, flaky or unbuilt test targets, e2e fixtures

labels.name: area/platform
labels.description: Platform/, Config/, Cli/ - service registration, config lookup, the CLI table

items.body:
#870 makes `FileTrust`'s POSIX acquisition case root-safe and, as root, it asserts the
delegation clause against a **real** root-owned `0640` file. That closes the failure. It
leaves a coverage gap this ticket is about, and the gap is only on hosts that are **not**
running the suite as root.

## The gap

`ClassifySecretFile`'s delegation clause — a group grant is an exposure only when the
owner is not administrative — is what keeps the documented arrangement from being
condemned. `0640 root:_fastcached` is what `InlineCredentialRejection` instructs and what
the macOS package ships, so the clause is load-bearing.

Where the suite runs unprivileged, that clause is exercised **only** through a synthesised
`SecretFileFacts`:

```cpp
CHECK(ClassifySecretFile({ .determined = true, .readableByGroup = true, .administrativelyOwned = true })
      == SecretExposure::None);
```

That covers the DECISION and says nothing about the ACQUISITION — whether
`ObserveSecretFile` actually reports `administrativelyOwned` for a real root-owned file.
The two are split deliberately and the split is right; this is about the half a
constructed record cannot reach.

Before #870 the case's own comment asserted this was unavoidable:

> The root-owned counterpart cannot be constructed without privileges, which is why the
> delegation clause is asserted through `ClassifySecretFile` above rather than only here.

## That sentence is false on Linux, measured

An unprivileged user namespace gives euid 0, and a file created inside it is genuinely
`uid=0` as `stat` reports it — which is exactly the fact `administrativelyOwned` reads
(`FileTrust.cpp`, `.administrativelyOwned = info.st_uid == 0`):

```
$ id -u
1000
$ unshare -r bash -c 'id -u; d=$(mktemp -d); : > $d/g.yaml; chmod 0640 $d/g.yaml; stat -c "uid=%u gid=%g mode=%a" $d/g.yaml'
0
uid=0 gid=0 mode=640
```

No sudo, no container, no privilege. The same facility reproduced #870's failure on an
unprivileged host, where the ticket had recorded it as reachable only by running the suite
as root.

## What is asked for

Exercise the real acquisition against a real root-owned `0640` file on hosts that are not
running as root, by re-executing the relevant case inside `unshare -r`.

**Every way of not being able to do it is an honest SKIP with a stated reason, never a
`SUCCEED` and never silence.** `.agent/rules/testing.md` covers this directly, and
`succeed-not-skip` will catch the wrong shape. The facility is absent or refused in at
least three ordinary situations, and none of them is a failure:

- macOS has no `unshare(1)` and no user namespaces;
- hardened kernels disable unprivileged user namespaces
  (`kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0`, `user.max_user_namespaces=0`);
- some container runtimes refuse nesting.

So the SKIP path is the common path on at least one platform CI builds, which means the
skip reason has to be specific enough to tell "this host cannot" from "this broke".

**And the namespace is not real root**, which is worth stating in the test rather than
leaving for a reader to discover: the file is `uid=0` only inside the namespace, and the
mapping is what makes that true. That is sufficient here — the code under test reads
`st_uid` and nothing else — and it would NOT be sufficient for a case that needed real
privilege, such as `SeedConfigFile`'s privileged branch.

## Not a defect, and deliberately not folded into #870

The classifier is correct, #870's case is correct once it is root-safe, and CI containers
that run as root already get this coverage. This is additional coverage for the
unprivileged host, which is why it is its own ticket rather than scope on a `type/test`
fix.

Related: #870 (the root-safety fix this builds on), #741 (which reached the privileged
branch with `unshare -r`).

items.title: util-linux: restore exec securebits after unshare/nsenter enter a user namespace
items.body:
## What

Adds `05-exec-aware-userns.patch` to the util-linux 2.42 series so that `unshare` and `nsenter` set the exec securebits again after creating or joining a user namespace. Closes #32.

## Why

The kernel resets a process's securebits to 0 when it creates or joins a user namespace, and that includes the locked bits. So `unshare --user -- python -c ...` ran without `EXEC_DENY_INTERACTIVE`, even under `setpriv --securebits +exec_deny_interactive,+exec_deny_interactive_locked`. I confirmed this on Linux 7.3.0: the bits read 0 after `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, and an unprivileged process can set them again.

## How

- Two new helpers in `lib/caputils.c`, which both tools already link: `get_exec_securebits()` saves `EXEC_RESTRICT_FILE`, `EXEC_DENY_INTERACTIVE`, and their locks. `restore_exec_securebits()` sets them again. If that fails it prints a warning and carries on, the same way exec-aware programs carry on when the securebits are unavailable.
- `unshare` calls them around `unshare()`.
- `nsenter` calls them around both `setns()` passes, before it changes UID/GID or forks.
- The `unshare(1)` and `nsenter(1)` man pages each get a note under `--user`.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Only the exec bits are restored.** Restoring `NOROOT` and the other bits would change what root can do in the new namespace, for example caps under `unshare -r`, so they stay as the kernel sets them.
- **No `CAP_SETPCAP` needed.** The kernel lets unprivileged processes set the exec bits, so the restore works whether or not the process has capabilities in the target namespace.
- If no exec bits were set, the helpers make no `PR_SET_SECUREBITS` call, so nothing changes for normal use or on kernels older than 6.14.

## Testing

- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.util-linux-exec-aware` passes all 13 cases. The new ones lock both exec bits and check `unshare --user`, `unshare --map-root-user`, and `nsenter --user --preserve-credentials` against a child in its own user namespace. They print SKIP if user namespaces aren't available. The `--map-root-user` case also prints SKIP, with the errno, if writing `uid_map` is denied. Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor userns restriction does that on the GitHub runners.
- Run against stock util-linux 2.42.4, the three new cases fail.
- The four existing patches export byte-identical from the stgit stack the new patch was made in.
- `nix fmt` and `reuse lint` pass.
- I did not run the full `nix flake check` or build on aarch64-linux.

## Problem

`tests/unit/adapters/test_workspace_fingerprint.py::test_a_pre_call_snapshot_is_never_published_into_a_store_re_created_during_its_walk` is flaky on a busy Linux host. It builds both stores with the real process-table probe (`lingering=lingering_process`, the default), unlike the file-walk tests, which use `_store()` and stub `lingering` to `False`. A same-user process started during the test's window, with a working directory or open files the probe cannot read, makes `other.effect_after(...)` read `unavailable` / `process_lingering` instead of `unchanged`:

```
later = WorkspaceEffectReading(effect='unavailable', reason='process_lingering', ...)
assert later.effect == "unchanged"
```

This is a test-isolation problem. The product rule is unchanged.

## Evidence (Linux, ext4, uid 1000, 8 vCPU box shared with other agents)

- Base `work/n7-reviewer-integrated` @ `2b12cc0b8`: 1 failure in 40 runs, alternating with the PR #1167 tree.
- PR #1167 tree: 3 failures in 40 runs in a separate loop; 0 in 40 when alternating with the base. The PR does not touch the lingering probe or this test.
- The whole file passes once: 127/127 on the base and 128/128 on the PR tree. Under a user-namespace root (`unshare -r`), `test_an_unreadable_directory_makes_the_comparison_unavailable` is skipped, as designed.
- Cursor's review of PR #1167 (comment 6326131199) reported three fingerprint test failures on its Linux VM, identical on parent `5bb84374e`. It did not name them. They could not be reproduced here apart from this flake.

## Proposed fix

Stub `lingering=lambda _window, _root: False` in every test of this file that is not about lingering itself (the revoke/re-grant, tally and consent tests that construct `WorkspaceFingerprintStore(...)` directly). Keep the real probe only in the `test_a_child_left_running_*` / `test_a_lingering_or_unknowable_process_table_is_unavailable` family. If Cursor's three failures are named later, add them here.

Found while triaging PR #1167 (v2 merge). Not caused by that PR. No FinishUP ledger coverage (dogfood service not available on the Boat controller).

items.title: PR 5: per-bot unix accounts + gateways, peer-bridge stream (swapdesign3 addendum)
items.body:
Implements **PR 5** of the swapdesign PR list: per-bot unix accounts with their own gateways (approved by Konrad 2026-10-24), plus the `bot-msg`/`peer-bridge` `stream` verb from swapdesign3 §3 and its addendum (a). Base: `main` 4323e1b. It doesn't depend on PR 1. This is code and tests only; nothing was provisioned on any box.

## What it does
- **`ops/hb-move <profile> … --shared-unit <unit>`** (journaled, `--dry-run`, `--undo`). It runs these steps in order:
  1. creates group `swarmhub-peer` and user `hb-<slug>` (home 0700, `~/.ssh` 0700);
  2. stops the shared gateway, copies the profile into the new account, renames the original to a numbered backup, and starts the shared gateway again;
  3. writes the root-owned registry entry in `/etc/swarmhub/bots.json`;
  4. installs `peer-bridge` and sudoers (checked with `visudo -cf`);
  5. starts `hermes-bot@<slug>` from its port drop-in and checks `/health`;
  6. installs the account's own webhook receiver and probes its port;
  7. renders the nginx snippet (`nginx -t`, then reload).

  `--undo` reverses each step, including from a half-done copy or retire. It never deletes anything.
- **`peer-bridge`** (sudo as root, `env_reset`, `!use_pty`):
  - The sender is the `SUDO_UID` account plus `--from-profile`. A dedicated account may send only as its own slug. `hermes` may send only as its own non-registry profiles, recorded `tier=shared` with a `(shared)` prefix. Anything else exits 77.
  - The bridge drops to the recipient before it reads any key. Root follows no planted symlink.
  - `held` and `durable` run the recipient's own skill.

items.title: Run ffprobe in the strict sandbox with the job's limits
items.body:
## Related Issue

- Closes #618
- Related / Depends on: #690 (job deadline and abort signal), #654 / #659 (ffprobe call count)

## Summary

- Problem: `ffprobe` parsed the uploaded file with a plain `execFileSync`: no user or network namespace, no resource limits, the worker's environment, and no link to the job deadline, even when `STRICT_SANDBOX` is on. A hostile container reached a native demuxer with network access.
- Outcome: every ffprobe run starts through the sandbox resolver with the same isolation as ffmpeg plus resource limits. A host that cannot confine the child answers 503 (`SandboxUnavailableError`) before ffprobe starts.

## Changes

- `runSandboxedBinarySync` (new, `process-sandbox.ts`): synchronous counterpart of `executeSandboxedBinary` for callers that cannot await. It uses `resolveSandboxedCommand` (so `unshare -r -n`, `prlimit`, and the strict refusal are the same code path), `shell: false`, the sanitized environment, closed stdin, a per-stream `maxBuffer`, a kill timeout, and the typed errors of the asynchronous runner. `nofile` is a new rlimit (`prlimit --nofile`).
- `media-ffprobe.ts`: both the JSON probe and the scalar probes run through `runSandboxedFfprobe`: network namespace, address space 4 GiB, CPU seconds = timeout, file size 1 MiB, 256 open files; the JSON report is capped at 4 MiB (scalar answers at 1 MiB); the timeout is `min(10 s, time left in the job)`; an aborted job starts nothing and rethrows its reason.
- `media-hdr.ts`: the MaxCLL probe, a second ffprobe call on the uploaded file, uses the same runner.
- `media.ts`: `probeMediaDuration` and the HDR probe no longer turn `SandboxUnavailableError` (or an abort) into "duration unknown" / "no light level".
- The probe functions take the conversion's options as an optional last argument (`signal` and the job deadline); every call site in the argument builders, the dropped-stream report, the loudness stage and the packaging path passes them. The number of ffprobe runs per conversion is unchanged.

## Scope

### Included

- All ffprobe spawn sites on uploaded input (`media-ffprobe.ts`, `media-hdr.ts`).
- Tests: argv/rlimit/env wiring on a simulated Linux host, 503 with no spawn, size cap, abort, deadline, and a real-namespace check on Linux.

### Excluded

- Other unsandboxed native spawns (listed below), which need their own issues.
- A PID namespace for ffprobe: ffmpeg does not use one either, and `unshare -p --fork` needs `--kill-child` handling for the timeout kill; left for a follow-up.
- Making the probes asynchronous. They run inside synchronous argument builders; an abort cannot interrupt a running probe (the event loop is blocked), only prevent the next one, and the deadline clamp bounds a running one.

### Spawn sites that still run outside `executeSandboxedBinary` / `resolveSandboxedCommand`

| Site | Input | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `archive.ts` `compressXz` / `decompressXz` (sync `execFileSync(xzBin)`) | uploaded bytes on stdin | unsandboxed, no rlimits; the async variant already uses `executeSandboxedBinary` |
| `media-ffmpeg-args.ts` `canOpenEncoderSession`, `-encoders` | none (lavfi source) | capability probes; the hardware session needs the GPU device |
| `media-hdr.ts` `ffmpeg -filters`, `media-audio-quality.ts` / `media.ts` `ffmpeg -version` | none | capability probes |
| `pdf-fonts.ts` `fc-list` | none | host font listing |
| `zstd.ts`, `archive.ts`, `media.ts` `which <tool>` | none | binary lookup |
| `storage/adapters/sftp.ts` `sftp` | customer credentials | needs the network by design |
| `process-sandbox.ts` `ps`, `unshare` capability probe | none | the sandbox's own probes |

## Verification

| Check | Command / Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Linter | `npm run lint` | Pass |
| Type check | `npx tsc --noEmit` (no errors in `src/` or the new tests) | Pass |
| Anti-cheat guard | `npm run guard:anti-cheat` (0 un-baselined violations) | Pass |
| Build | `npm run build` | Pass |
| New tests | `npx vitest run tests/media-ffprobe-sandbox-wiring.test.ts tests/media-ffprobe-sandbox-limits.test.ts` (macOS: Linux namespace test skipped) | Pass |
| Media suites | 42 media/HDR/WAV/MP4/resampler files under `ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1`, identical failure set on this branch and on `origin/main` (macOS lacks `libvorbis`, `zscale` etc.) | Same as base |
| ffprobe call count | `tests/media-video-transcode-overhead.test.ts`, `tests/media-audio-encode-overhead.test.ts`: zero ffprobe processes for WAV and plain MP4 as before | Pass |
| Family map | `git diff --name-only origin/main \| node scripts/ci-parity-families.mjs` maps to all families (shared `process-sandbox.ts`), nothing unclassified | Pass |
| Speed | `convertWithNativeFfmpeg` on a probe-needing mp3 and mkv input, 12 runs, median ms base to branch: mp3 to flac 79.4 to 80.3, mp3 to aac 132.6 to 133.5, mkv to mp4 102.3 to 103.0 (macOS, no namespace wrapper) | Pass |

### Not Run

- The Linux-only paths (real `unshare -r -n`, `prlimit`) and the strict 503 suite were not run locally: the development host is macOS and Docker is unavailable. They run in CI (`tests/media-ffprobe-sandbox-limits.test.ts` checks the net namespace, uid map and device list of a spy ffprobe).
- The two extra exec hops of the wrapper were measured with a stand-in (two `env` hops): about +1.5 ms per ffprobe run (21.4 ms to 23.0 ms) against an ffmpeg run of 80 ms or more.

## Risk & Delivery

- Risk: Medium
- Main risk: the 4 GiB address-space limit on a many-core host with heavy frame threading could make a legitimate probe fail; the failure is a `ConversionFailedError`, not a silent default. The limit is a constant in `media-ffprobe.ts`.
- Rollout / rollback / recovery: Not required

## Review Guide

- Review first: `runSandboxedBinarySync` in `src/lib/security/process-sandbox.ts`, then `runSandboxedFfprobe` in `src/lib/conversions/media-ffprobe.ts`.
- Key decision / trade-off: the runner is synchronous because the argument builders are; the cost is that an abort cannot interrupt a running probe, which the deadline clamp bounds.

## Checklist

- [x] All automated tests and linter pass locally (Linux-only suites run in CI).
- [ ] Claude Code review findings are addressed and all review threads are resolved.
- [x] Changes match acceptance criteria of the related issue.
- [x] No extraneous files or secrets included.
- [ ] If a conversion family changed: `parity quality` passes, and the `automerge` label has been added so `parity speed` runs on the final commit.

items.title: Fix pbs upgrade bugs, add backup run lock, add test suite
items.body:
## Summary

**`pbs upgrade` fixes**
- **Temp dir and exit code.** The `EXIT` trap referenced a `local` variable that is out of scope once the function returns, so under `set -u` it failed with `tmp: unbound variable`. As a result, every `pbs upgrade` exited 1, even when it succeeded, and left a `pbs-upgrade.*` dir in `/tmp`. The trap now expands the path when it is set, and `upgrade.sh`'s exit code is passed through. `mktemp` also respects `TMPDIR` now.
- **Commit SHAs as `PBS_UPGRADE_REF`.** The help text promised these, but `git clone --branch` rejects SHAs. The script now falls back to `git init`, then `git fetch --depth 1 <sha>`, then `checkout FETCH_HEAD`. The SHA must be the full SHA.

**Backup run lock**
- `run-backup.sh` holds a non-blocking `flock` on `/run/lock/pbs-backup.lock` for the whole run. A second run (for example, a manual `pbs run-backup` while the timer's run is in progress) exits with code **3** and runs neither the hooks nor the backup.
- Hooks are started with the lock fd closed. Otherwise a hook that leaves a process running would hold the lock forever.
- The README now documents the exit codes: 0 ok, 1 backup failed, 2 missing config, 3 already running.

**Tests and CI**
- `tests/run.sh` is a test harness that needs nothing beyond bash. Locally it runs under `unshare -r` (fake root, no real privileges); in GitHub Actions it runs as real root via `sudo`. Tests only write under their own temp dirs, and `proxmox-backup-client`, `apt-mark`, `dpkg`, `logger` and the upstream `upgrade.sh` are all stubbed.
- There are 16 tests: smoke tests, `pbs upgrade` (branch/tag/SHA refs, exit code passthrough, temp-dir cleanup, prompt handling) and `run-backup.sh` (success, failure, missing config, concurrent runs, hook-spawned daemons).
- To make `run-backup.sh` testable, `PBS_ETC_DIR` and `PBS_LOCK_FILE` overrides were added. Production defaults are unchanged.

**Version:** bumped to 1.1.1 so installed hosts pick this up via `pbs upgrade`.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/run.sh`: all 16 pass, 5 consecutive runs, no leftover temp dirs
- [x] The new tests fail on the pre-fix code: the upgrade tests with `unbound variable` / `Remote branch <sha> not found`, the concurrency test with the second run exiting 0, and the hook-daemon test with exit 3

items.title: feat(run-spaceapp): support rootless Podman as a container engine (#63)
items.body:
Closes #63

## Problem and user impact

Many Linux developers and enterprise environments (Fedora, RHEL, CentOS Stream, Debian, Ubuntu, and Arch-family distributions) run rootless Podman (`podman` + `podman compose`) instead of a rootful Docker daemon so container engines do not require root privileges on the host. Previously, `run-spaceapp` hardcoded `docker` across CLI execution, readiness checks, storage inspection, and workspace permission hints.

## Change

- **Engine resolution & config schema (`packages/run-spaceapp/src/index.mjs`)**:
  - Add `CONTAINER_ENGINES = Object.freeze(["docker", "podman"])`, `resolveContainerEngine(requestedEngine, existingEngine)`, and optional `containerEngine` persistence in `config.json` (`validateConfig`, `createDefaultConfig`, `prepareInstallation`).
  - Update `composeCommand(action, root, options)` to return `{ command: engine, args }` for `"docker"` or `"podman"`.
  - Add `podmanUnshareChownArgs(hostPath, { uid, gid })` to construct safe, shell-free `podman unshare chown -R 10001:10001 <path>` arguments for rootless UID/GID mapping.
- **Engine detection & prerequisites (`packages/run-spaceapp/src/prerequisites.mjs`)**:
  - Add `podmanCliAndComposeAreAvailable`, `podmanIsReady`, `detectContainerEngine`, and rootless Podman verification in `ensureDockerAvailable` when `podman` is selected (`--engine podman` or `SPACEAPP_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman`) or when Docker is absent.
- **Storage plan inspection (`packages/run-spaceapp/src/storage.mjs`)**:
  - Inspect images and host resources using the active engine (`podman` or `docker`), supporting rootless Podman `info --format {{json .}}` fields (`host.arch`, `host.cpus`, `host.memTotal`, and `store.graphRoot`).
- **CLI lifecycle, workspace hints & doctor diagnostics (`packages/run-spaceapp/src/cli.mjs`)**:
  - Add `podman` to `trustedCommands` and `spawnTrustedCommand` (`shell: false`), and accept `--engine <auto|docker|podman>` (or `SPACEAPP_CONTAINER_ENGINE`).
  - Route lifecycle commands (`up`, `down`, `status`, `logs`, `doctor`, `backup`, `restore`, `update`, `uninstall`) through the configured or selected container engine.
  - Print rootless `podman unshare chown -R 10001:10001` instructions instead of `sudo setfacl` when adding writable workspaces under Podman on Linux.
- **Tests, CI & Documentation**:
  - Add unit and lifecycle test suite in `packages/run-spaceapp/tests/podman.test.mjs`.
  - Add `podman-rootless` CI job on `ubuntu-latest` in `.github/workflows/platform-matrix.yml`.

Every external command (`aws`, `btrfs`, `age`, `lz4`, `mbuffer`, `openssl`, `date`, `sudo`) is replaced by a stub on `PATH`, so the suite needs neither a btrfs filesystem nor an AWS account. The scripts refuse to run as anything but root, so `tests/run.sh` re-executes itself under `unshare -r`. CI runs it as root instead.

items.title: Update syscall allowlist
Keep Apple Silicon on Omarchy's Quickshell build for the Qt 6.11 import patch
items.body:
Qt 6.12 (now in Arch Linux ARM) adds a `Color` singleton to `QtQuick` that shadows the `qs.Commons` `Color`. As a result, `Color.*` resolves as `undefined` in the shell **and in every plugin**, so plugins paint white or black regardless of the theme.

#710 and #723 qualify `Color` as `Commons.Color` inside `shell/`, but third-party plugins under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins` keep the unqualified reference and stay broken. Upstream fixed this once for everything with a load-time patch instead, and this PR ports that approach.

### Why ARM installs end up with the wrong Quickshell

The patch only works with Omarchy's Quickshell build. On ARM, `arm-package-sources.sh` keeps `[omarchy]` at `Usage = Sync`. That is intentional: only explicitly selected packages come from it. So any unqualified `quickshell` resolves to Arch's build, which ignores the pragma. That includes the original install, `pacman -Syu`, and migration `1787399318`'s `pacman -S quickshell`. This affects every ARM install, not only older `pacman.conf` files.

A one-off migration alone would not keep it fixed:

- `pacman -Syu` never upgrades from `[omarchy]`, so later Omarchy builds (e.g. omacom/omarchy-pkgs#1272) would never arrive.
- Once Arch ships a Quickshell version that sorts newer than `0.3.2.r7…`, the next update would replace Omarchy's build with Arch's, and the palette breaks again.
- `omarchy refresh pacman` runs `-Syyuu`, which today downgrades Omarchy's build back to Arch's `0.3.2-1`.

Upstream Omarchy does not hit this. Its `default/pacman/aarch64-apple/pacman-edge.conf` lists `[omarchy]` first without `Usage = Sync`, so `quickshell` resolves to Omarchy's build without being selected. The problem is specific to this fork's selective-edge policy.

### Depends on #741

On `quattro` today, `omarchy update` on Apple Silicon fails before any package is upgraded, because edge no longer publishes `hyprtoolkit` or `hyprland-guiutils` for aarch64 (omacom/omarchy-pkgs#853). It fails with `target not found: hyprtoolkit`. While that holds, no package or migration from this PR can reach a Mac. #742 and #747 both fix it, and both touch `omarchy_arm_package_targets`. Whichever lands first, I'll rebase this onto it. With #747 that means adding `quickshell` to its package loop. With #742 the change below applies as is, and its availability filter also covers the case where edge ever drops `quickshell`.

### Changes

- **`shell/shell.qml`:** add `//@ pragma OmarchyLoadPatch`, ported from omacom/omarchy#14845. Omarchy's Quickshell build (`pkgs.omarchy.org`, from omacom/omarchy-pkgs#935) then rewrites unversioned `import QtQuick` to `6.11` in every QML file it loads, plugins included. Stock Quickshell treats the pragma as an unrecognized comment.
- **`install/helpers/arm-package-sources.sh`:** add `omarchy/quickshell` to `omarchy_arm_package_targets`, next to the Hyprland stack. The installer, `omarchy update`, `omarchy refresh pacman` and `fix-arm-packages.sh` now request it explicitly. `omarchy_arm_package_upgrade_args` adds it to `--ignore`, so a newer Arch build cannot replace it in the same sysupgrade. The default-package loop in `install.sh` already skips selected packages, so `yay` never gets an unqualified `quickshell`.
- **Migration `1792350611.sh`:** if the installed Quickshell isn't Omarchy's build (`quickshell --version` lacks `distributed by Omarchy`), install `omarchy/quickshell`. It is still needed because the first `omarchy update` after this ships runs the previous helper. Following `1784672586.sh`, it exits cleanly when `[omarchy]` cannot serve the package, and `--ask 4` replaces a leftover `quickshell-git` in place.
- **Tests:** `arm-package-sources`, `arm-package-transaction`, `arm-package-recovery`, `update-package-conflict` and `test/vm/run-selective-edge` now expect `omarchy/quickshell`. The real-pacman transaction fixture includes a newer `extra/quickshell` and asserts it is not selected. The new `quickshell-load-patch-migration-test.sh` runs the migration against stubs in all three cases: Omarchy's build is a no-op, Arch's build is replaced, and an unavailable package is skipped. It also asserts `shell.qml` keeps the pragma. Making the migration install unqualified `quickshell`, as `1787399318` does, fails it. `aarch64-packages-test.sh` checks the migration's availability guard.
- **Docs:** `docs/arm-package-sources.md` lists Quickshell among the selected packages and explains why. The volunteer checklist collects `quickshell --version`.

Companion fix: omacom/omarchy-pkgs#1272 extends the patch to unversioned `import QtQuick.Window`, which re-exports the latest QtQuick and otherwise brings `Color` back (e.g. `b.omashot`, and `shell/Ui/MultiSelect.qml`).

### Every path to Arch's Quickshell

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh install (`install.sh`, also via `omarchy-mac-setup`) | the default-package loop installs unqualified `quickshell` from `extra` | the compatibility transaction installs `omarchy/quickshell`, and the loop skips selected packages |
| Existing install, `omarchy update` | sysupgrade keeps Arch's build forever | the first update (still on the old helper) runs the migration, and later updates select `omarchy/quickshell` |
| `omarchy refresh pacman` (`-Syyuu`) | downgrades Omarchy's build to `extra/quickshell 0.3.2-1` | selects `omarchy/quickshell` |
| `fix-arm-packages.sh` recovery | fetches the helper from `quattro` without `quickshell` | fetches the helper from `quattro` with `quickshell` |
| 3.x → Quattro (`omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro-mac`) | installs unqualified `quickshell`, and `[omarchy]` is not configured yet | the migration skips; the first `omarchy update` adds `[omarchy]` and selects `omarchy/quickshell` |
| Leftover `quickshell-git` (no load patch) | kept | the migration replaces it with `--ask 4` (checked in a real transaction under `unshare -r`). A later update with only `--noconfirm` would stop on the conflict prompt, which the update conflict handler hands to the user. |
| Newer Arch `quickshell` | replaces Omarchy's build on the next sysupgrade | ignored through `--ignore quickshell` |

Not covered here, and tracked elsewhere:

- `shell/Ui/MultiSelect.qml` and third-party plugins with an unversioned `import QtQuick.Window` get `Color` back even with the pragma. omacom/omarchy-pkgs#1272 handles that for every plugin. #710, #723 and #745 also qualify `MultiSelect.qml` as `Commons.Color`.
- A plugin that launches its own Quickshell root (its own `shell.qml`) needs the pragma in that root. `shell/shell.qml` is the only root this repo ships.

### Verification (MacBook, qt6-declarative 6.12.0)

- **Arch's quickshell 0.3.2-1, the state an `omarchy update` left this machine in:** `quickshell --version` reports `distributed by Arch Linux`. The bar, Control Panel and plugins render white, and one boot logged more than 29,000 `Unable to assign [undefined] to QColor` warnings across built-in and third-party plugins.
- **`omarchy/quickshell` 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-1 + pragma:** after `omarchy restart shell`, the new shell process logs no palette warnings, and the shell and plugins follow the theme again.
- **Package resolution with real pacman** (copy of this machine's local database, live `pkgs.omarchy.org/edge/aarch64` database from 2026-10-21, `-Su --needed -p`, using the #741 target set plus this PR):

  | Installed quickshell | #741 alone | #741 + this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Arch `0.3.2-1` | quickshell untouched (stays Arch's) | `omarchy/quickshell 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-2` |
  | Omarchy `0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-1` | quickshell untouched (the `-2` rebuild never arrives) | `omarchy/quickshell 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-2` |

  `omarchy refresh pacman` (`-Suu`) with Omarchy's build installed and without this PR selects `extra/quickshell 0.3.2-1`, which is a downgrade back to Arch's build.
- **Migration:** covered by `quickshell-load-patch-migration-test.sh`. A real `pacman -S --noconfirm --ask 4 omarchy/quickshell` in an `unshare -r` fake root with `quickshell-git` installed removes `quickshell-git` and installs `quickshell 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-2`. The same transaction without `--ask 4` fails with `unresolvable package conflicts detected`.
- `./test/all`: 291 of 297 shell test files pass. The other 6 fail identically on `quattro` without this change, because of the environment (tmpfs cache, no omarchy-pkgs checkout, host units). `bin/omarchy commands --check` and the `bin/` syntax check pass.
- `arm-package-recovery-test.sh` passes with `/usr/share/omarchy` hidden. On a machine with Omarchy installed, `fix-arm-packages.sh` picks the installed helper before the fetched one, so that test's "fetched helper" case checks the installed copy instead. That issue already exists and is separate from this PR.

### Risk

Quickshell builds against Qt's private QML API, which is why Arch rebuilds it for every Qt release. Pinning the Omarchy build means a Qt bump in Arch Linux ARM needs a matching `pkgs.omarchy.org` aarch64 rebuild. x86 Omarchy already has the same dependency, because `[omarchy]` is listed first there.

items.title: Fresh procfs mount in a user namespace reveals paths hidden by locked mounts
items.body:
A process in a mount namespace owned by a child user namespace can mount a fresh procfs and read through it the files its own /proc hides behind a locked mount. 

Linux refuses that mount in mount_too_revealing(), but the sentry has no such check (MountAt in pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go). The same goes for sysfs, and for a read-write proc mount while /proc is locked read-only.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
mkdir -p /tmp/p
unshare -m sh -c '
mount --make-rprivate /
mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /proc/sys
unshare -U -r -m -p -f sh -c "mount -t proc proc /tmp/p && ls /tmp/p/sys"
'
echo "exit=$?"
```

On Linux the inner mount fails:

```
mount: /tmp/p: permission denied.
exit=32
```

Under runsc it succeeds and the new mount shows what the tmpfs was hiding:

```
fs
kernel
net
user
vm
exit=0
```

</details>

Proposed fix in #15513.

items.title: fix(online): load task artifacts with restricted unpickler
items.body:
## Description

`RollingStrategy` read the `task` artifact of every recorder with `recorder.load_object("task")`, which falls back to `MLflowRecorder.load_object`'s default `pickle.Unpickler`. All four call sites now pass `unpickler=RestrictedUnpickler` (`qlib/utils/pickle_utils.py`), the same whitelist-based unpickler already used elsewhere in the repo (`qlib/data/cache.py`, `qlib/workflow/task/manage.py`, ...).

```
-task_config = recorder.load_object("task")
+task_config = recorder.load_object("task", unpickler=RestrictedUnpickler)
```

Task configs are plain dicts of strings/numbers plus pandas `Timestamp` segments, all of which the existing whitelist allows, so legitimate rolling workflows are unaffected.

## Motivation and Context

`prepare_tasks` / `_list_latest` / `get_collector`'s `rec_key` run automatically during online and rolling preparation. When the MLflow tracking server or experiment holds untrusted artifacts, an attacker-supplied `task` artifact reaches `pickle.Unpickler.load()` with no restriction, giving arbitrary code execution inside the workflow process — no victim interaction required.

Attack path: `malicious task artifact -> prepare_tasks/_list_latest -> load_object("task") -> pickle load -> RCE`.

## Validation

PoC: a `task` artifact whose `__reduce__` invokes `os.system` to write a `PWNED` marker, logged to a local MLflow file store and read back through `RollingStrategy._list_latest`.

```
RUNTIME VALIDATION [PRE-FIX]: EXPLOIT SUCCEEDED - malicious 'task' pickle executed os.system and wrote /tmp/poc_sandbox.ewjrBf/PWNED
RUNTIME VALIDATION [POST-FIX]: EXPLOIT BLOCKED - blocked by restricted unpickler: LoadObjectError; no PWNED marker written
RUNTIME VALIDATION [REGRESSION]: 4 passed, 0 failed (tests/test_workflow.py tests/data_mid_layer_tests/test_handler.py tests/misc/test_utils.py)
SANDBOX VALIDATION: unshare network+user namespace subprocess, sandbox dirs /tmp/poc_sandbox.ewjrBf (pre-fix) and /tmp/poc_sandbox.EVFIJq (post-fix) - payload effect observed pre-fix: yes, post-fix: no
```

Sandbox setup used (identical command for both runs, only the fix differed):

```
SB=$(mktemp -d /tmp/poc_sandbox.XXXXXX)
POC_SANDBOX=$SB MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE=true PYTHONPATH=/home/ubuntu/repos/qlib \
  unshare -r -n python poc_strategy_pickle.py
```

The PoC ran with no network namespace (`unshare -n`), in a throwaway directory, with `HOME` redirected into the sandbox and AWS credential env vars cleared; the MLflow backend was a local file store inside the sandbox dir. The payload only wrote a harmless `PWNED` marker.

A benign task config (including pandas `Timestamp` test segments) was also loaded through `RestrictedUnpickler` successfully to confirm no functional regression.

Follow-up fixes for the five P2 findings in `jobroute-xrev2-verdict.md` (second independent review of #6 at `31e22ad`). Base: `feat/hermes-jobroute`. **Do not merge without review.** Nothing was installed, parked or activated.

## Fixes (each with tests)

1. **Full undo after real use.** `uninstall.py` (README step 4) now always removes `state/jobroute/.lock` and `profiles/<profile>.jsonl`, plus a stale `install-state.new`. Only regular files we own are removed. `audit.jsonl` still goes only with `--remove-audit`. Tests: `test_full_rollback_after_real_submit_matches_baseline[fresh|populated]` and `test_rollback_without_remove_audit_keeps_only_the_audit_log`. The exact-installer rollback harness now submits through the installed route before running the documented undo.
2. **Exec trust check before every launch** (`jobroute_trust.py`). The check covers `sb_codejob`, the engine found on the route `path`, the real path of each, every ancestor directory and every PATH entry. Each must be owned by the route user or by root and must not be group/world-writable. Root-owned sticky dirs such as `/tmp` are allowed. PATH entries must be absolute with no `..`. Anything else is refused with an audited `error` row and nothing runs. The engine is passed to sb-codejob as the absolute path that was checked. Tests cover a writable sb-codejob or its dir, a writable engine or PATH dir, a symlink to an untrusted real path, a writable ancestor, relative/empty/`..` PATH entries, a missing engine, the MCP path, and owner/sticky unit rules.
3. **Reservation before the slow launch** (`jobroute_jobs.py`). The index reservation row and the audit `launching` row are written under the lock before sb-codejob runs. The lock is no longer held across the launch, and its wait is capped at 5 s (`route busy`, exit 3). A killed or timed-out launch keeps its reservation, which counts toward the limits. Once the launcher is gone (pid + start time), the reservation is matched to the job's status file (same label, engine argv and workdir, within 5 min), and the route writes a `recover` index row and audit row. A clean launch failure is closed as `failed`. items.title: `eoc --latest` crashes with a raw stack trace when Maven Central is unreachable
items.body:
## What happens

`src/parser-version.js`'s `get()` (lines 16-29) does a synchronous request to Maven Central and neither catches transport errors nor handles a non-200 response gracefully - it just throws. It is called from `src/eoc.js:115` at module load time, which is before `program.parseAsync()` runs and therefore outside the top-level `try/catch` at `src/eoc.js:439-446`. So nothing in the process can catch whatever it throws.

Its sibling function `exists()` was explicitly hardened for exactly this scenario in #998 and #1085 (warn and proceed instead of crashing), but `get()` never received the same treatment.

Reproduced in a network namespace with only external network removed (loopback still up):

```
$ unshare -r -n sh -c 'ip link set lo up; node src/eoc.js --latest lint'
node_modules/sync-rpc/lib/index.js:167
    throw error;
    ^
Error
    at extractValue (.../sync-rpc/lib/index.js:165:19)
    at Object.get (src/parser-version.js:20:17)
    at Object.<anonymous> (src/eoc.js:115:40)
    ...
  code: 'ENETUNREACH'
```

Note the thrown error has an empty `message`, so even moving the call inside a try/catch would only print a blank line - the fix needs to be inside `get()` itself, catching the transport error and falling back the same way `exists()` does.

## What should happen

`eoc --latest` should behave gracefully when Maven Central is unreachable - warn and fall back to the bundled parser version (mirroring what `exists()` already does), not print a raw Node internal stack trace with an empty error message.

items.title: Sinden Lightgun: UVC modules + driver runtime, fetched on device
items.body:
## Summary

Support for the [Sinden Lightgun](https://www.sindenlightgun.com/), a camera light gun for LCDs, requested by a user. Main_MiSTer already recognises the guns (`input.cpp`, "Sinden Lightgun"). What was missing is the host-side driver that turns the gun's camera feed into an aim point, and the kernel driver for that camera.

- **Kernel:** USB video class (`uvcvideo`) built as modules on the DE10 config, mirrored into the common fragment. RT 7.2 inherits it, and the DE25 resolves the same delta. Stock never had a camera driver, which is why the community Sinden package swaps in its own 5.15 kernel.
- **`package/sinden-lightgun`** (DE10 defconfig): a udev rule plus `/usr/sbin/mister-sinden-lightgun`. The driver runs while a gun's camera is present, is pinned to **CPU0** (Main is on CPU1), and restarts when the gun count changes.
- **On-device download, not redistribution:** Sinden's licence lets only Sinden distribute its driver, so the image carries none of it. `Scripts/sinden_lightgun.sh` downloads the official V2.08b zip from sindenlightgun.com (pinned sha256) and unpacks the Raspberry Pi build to `/media/fat/linux/sinden/`. The script is registered in install/uninstall/updater/sdcard payload/lint like the other companion Scripts.
- **Everything the driver links against comes from Buildroot:** mono 6.12, SDL 1.2, SDL_image 1.2, and a new `package/libjpeg62`. That package builds Buildroot's own jpeg-turbo tarball with the 6.2 ABI next to the system `libjpeg.so.8`; symbol versions keep the two apart, and it verifies against Buildroot's `jpeg-turbo.hash`. Sinden's two wrapper `.so` files can't be replaced, because the licence forbids decompiling.
- **Mono trim:** Buildroot's mono puts 200 MB on the target. A finalize hook keeps the runtime plus the 8 assemblies `LightgunMono.exe` references, about 20 MB. It is an option (default y) because it would break any other mono user. The rootfs goes from 333 to 355 MB, within the size budget.

Rationale and details: `docs/sinden-lightgun.md`.

## Testing

In qemu-arm on the built `rootfs.tar` (`unshare -r chroot`):
- The installer downloads, verifies and unpacks the zip with BusyBox `unzip`/`sha256sum`.
- `LightgunMono.exe joystick mediumresource` on the **trimmed** mono starts and runs its gun search ("Number of Sinden Lightguns Found 0"). That run caught the first trim layout, which broke startup; framework assemblies must stay in `gac/`.
- A probe on the same runtime reads the config through `ConfigurationManager`, resolves both Sinden `.so` files via P/Invoke, and opens a `SerialPort` through `libMonoPosixHelper`.
- Start/stop/reconcile with a stand-in process: no lock fd inherited, CPU affinity 0, no hang with 0 guns, stale-PID guard works, and unknown args are dropped and logged.
- `check-defconfigs.sh` OK, `check-linux-img.sh` passes, and shellcheck is clean. `ci-tests.sh`: 464 pass. The 2 local failures come from stale state in my `output/` (two kernel build dirs, and pre-#216 firmware stamps), not from this branch.

**Not tested: anything with a real gun.** That includes the udev rule firing on the gun, `uvcvideo` streaming its MJPEG, whether `mediumresource` keeps up on the A9, and aim. Nobody on the project owns one, so this needs the requesting user. A code review ran on the branch; its findings are fixed in the last commit.

## Not in this PR

The driver needs a **white border** on screen, and cores don't draw one. Today that means the community `*-Sinden.rbf` core forks. Users must **not** run that package's installer on this image, because it replaces `zImage_dtb` with a 5.15 kernel. A generic fix would wire the scaler's unused `o_border` colour (`sys/ascal.vhd`) to a Main-settable register, combined with the existing `vscale_border` option. That is an upstream Template_MiSTer + Main_MiSTer change (doc §7).

items.body:
## Leaderboard Submission: `3R-Cond`

- **Track:** `semi-adaptive` (2–3 Parallel Rounds)
- **Authors:** Farrokh Labib (Unitary Foundation, `@FarLab`)
- **Entrypoint:** `submission.py:SemiAdapt3RCondSubmission`

### Mechanism
Designed for hardware regimes where classical feedback latency restricts execution to 2–3 parallel circuit batches:
1. **Round 1 (Coarse Localization)**: Executes a lean $r = 1.50$ geometric ladder up to $n_{L-3} \approx 0.30\,n_{\max}$ in a single parallel batch (~38% of total budget), localizing $\hat\theta_1$ and identifying the top rival modes.
2. **Round 2 (Opposite-Slope Deep Batch + Rival Killer)**: Selects the top 3 deep rungs ($n_{L-2}, n_{L-1}, n_L$) in parallel to sit on **complementary opposite-slope quadrature targets** ($+\phi_0$ and $-\phi_0 \pmod{\pi}$) while maximizing Bhattacharyya separation against Round-1 rivals.
3. **Round 3 (Conditional Tie-Breaker on ~19% of Trials)**: Only if the post-Round-2 log-likelihood gap $\Delta\ell_2 < 4.5$, fires a 2-shot targeted tie-breaker batch.

items.title: detect: `timeout` / `nohup` / `nice` などの prefix wrapper が peel されない (architecture.md の記述と実装が乖離)
items.body:
## 概要 (High)

`docs/design/architecture.md` には「rule / plugin DSL は評価前に `unwrap_all_prefix_wrappers` で `sudo` / `env` / `timeout` 等の prefix を全層 peel する」とあり、`src/facts/shell.rs` の doc comment にも `sudo env timeout cmd` の例がある。しかし `PREFIX_WRAPPERS` (`src/facts/shell.rs:292`) に登録されているのは `sudo` / `doas` / `pkexec` / `run0` / `env` / `command` だけで、**`timeout` は含まれていない**。ほかに一般的な exec 系 wrapper も未対応で、hardDeny を素通りする。

## 再現 (HEAD 5a3d91a)

すべて `Decision: allow` になる:

```text
timeout 5 rm -rf /
timeout 5 git push --force origin main
nohup rm -rf /
nohup cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa            # 比較: `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` は ask
nice -n 10 rm -rf /
stdbuf -o0 rm -rf /
ionice -c3 rm -rf /
setsid rm -rf /
unshare -r rm -rf /
chroot / rm -rf /
flock /tmp/l rm -rf /
busybox rm -rf /
watch rm -rf /
script -c "rm -rf /"
parallel rm -rf ::: /
```

## 期待値

wrapper を peel した内側のコマンドで判定する。上の例は `rm -rf /` / `git push --force` と同じく deny (`cat` は ask) になるべき。

## 修正方針案

- `PREFIX_WRAPPERS` に次を追加する (各 wrapper の value 付きフラグも定義する):
  - `timeout` (先頭の位置引数 DURATION を 1 つ読み飛ばす。`-s`/`-k` は値付き)
  - `nohup`、`setsid`、`time` (`/usr/bin/time`)
  - `nice` (`-n`)、`ionice` (`-c`/`-n`/`-p`)、`stdbuf` (`-i`/`-o`/`-e`)
  - `chroot` (NEWROOT の位置引数を 1 つ読み飛ばす)、`flock` (LOCKFILE の位置引数を 1 つ読み飛ばす。`-c` は `bash -c` 扱い)
  - `unshare`、`busybox` (次の語を applet 名として head にする)
- `watch` / `script -c` / `parallel` は引数を文字列として連結して実行するため、`bash -c` と同じく `inner_argv` に再 parse する
- architecture.md の記述は実装に合わせて具体化する
- corpus に must_catch を追加する

## mutation testing との関連

`unwrap_prefix_wrapper` (341-391 行) は caught が多い一方、wrapper の **網羅性** は mutation では検出できない (リストにない要素は変異しない)。このためドキュメント側からの差分チェックが必要。

items.title: lane launch: a local lane's commands cannot write outside the lane's own paths or reach the live session's sockets unless its item declares the need

labels.name: skills
labels.description: skills/, agents/, skill-templates/, and base agent instructions

items.body:
A lane started on an owner machine runs its commands under a mount boundary. The lane can write only its worktree, its repository's git directory, its harness's state and its lane state. It cannot reach the live desktop's sockets unless its item declares the need.

- **Today:** a local lane's commands can write every path the owner can write. `LANE_LAUNCH_SCRUB` clears three display names (KEN-4185). Its own comment names what stays reachable: the `wayland-0` fallback, a tool's own socket such as ydotool's, and a pane the lane opens on its tmux server. A job the lane starts through `lib/job-unit.sh` (`systemd-run --user`) runs outside the lane.
- **After:** `open-terminal` starts a local lane's process tree in a user and mount namespace. The rest of the host is read-only. The live compositor and input-tool sockets are hidden unless the lane was launched with `--live-display`. A job unit the lane starts runs inside the same boundary.

**Reached by**: every local lane on an owner machine. On 2026-10-21, a vgshell lane's own probe command (VGS-1969) deleted that lane's checkout. That is a write no consumer's test boundary can stop, because the lane's own command made it. vgshell filed the boundary for its own test runs as VGS-1971 and VGS-1972 (https://linear.app/vanillagreen/issue/VGS-1971); that covers the test-run part of the same morning's incidents, not a lane's own commands.

## Done when

- [ ] A launch-suite row starts a local lane and, from inside it, removes a disposable directory outside the lane's writable set. The removal fails, and the directory stays intact. Its must-fail control is today's launcher, under which the removal succeeds.
- [ ] Inside a lane launched without `--live-display`, a socket planted in a scratch `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` under a Wayland or Hyprland name is not reachable. With `--live-display` it is reachable, and the lane record names that declaration.
- [ ] A job that the lane starts through `lib/job-unit.sh` meets the same refusal as the lane itself.
- [ ] Inside a lane, `bwrap --ro-bind / / true` and `unshare -r true` both succeed.

## Requirements

- The writable set is the lane's worktree, the repository's git common directory, the lane's harness state, kendex lane state, and any paths the consumer declares.
- Allow nested user namespaces (no `--disable-userns`), so a consumer's own test boundary, bwrap and `unshare` still start inside a lane.
- One launch-time declaration, `--live-display`, as KEN-4185 defined it. No second scrub list.
- Hosted lanes are out of scope, because they already run in their own sandbox.

## Filing record

**Source**: Jarvis, the owner's delegate, owner note 1792604556 (2026-10-21), from vgshell's test-run boundary design read.
**Evidence**: the VGS-1969 lane notice 1792600362-117884-5828 (a probe deleted the lane's checkout) and the residuals that KEN-4185 names in `LANE_LAUNCH_SCRUB`'s comment.
**Location**: `skills/orch/scripts/open-terminal`, `skills/orch/scripts/lib/lane-launch.sh`, `skills/orch/scripts/lib/job-unit.sh`, `skills/orch/tests/`

items.title: SECURITY: webmin accepts root with an empty password before first boot completes
items.body:
**Filed in the private handbook deliberately. `Keel-Linux/common`, `inithooks`
and `tracker` are public; this must not be described there until it is fixed.**

Between the moment an appliance boots and the moment `firstboot.d/30rootpass`
completes, Webmin accepts **root with an empty password** on port 12321.

## The mechanism, each link verified

1. `common/conf/turnkey.d/rootpass` ships, when `ROOT_PASS` is unset at build
   time, which is the normal case:

       # this is a blank password
       usermod -p U6aMy0wojraho root

2. `U6aMy0wojraho` is **a valid DES hash of the empty string**, not a locked
   account. Computed independently:

       crypt("", "U6")  ->  U6aMy0wojraho     matches what the build writes
       crypt("x", "U6") ->  U6QAAaFC1TvPI

   A locked account would carry `!` or `*`. This one matches an empty
   submitted password by ordinary comparison, so `nullok` below is a second
   independent weakening rather than the cause.

3. Verified on two live containers: `/etc/pam.d/webmin` is
   `auth required pam_unix.so nullok`; `/etc/webmin/miniserv.conf` has
   `passwd_mode=0` and **no `allow=`**; `/etc/webmin/miniserv.users` is
   `root:x:0`; miniserv binds `0.0.0.0:12321` **and `[::]:12321`**;
   `WEBMIN_FW_TCP_INCOMING` opens 12321; `systemctl is-enabled webmin` is
   enabled; `miniserv.pl` contains no empty-password guard.

SSH is not affected: `PermitRootLogin yes`, but OpenSSH defaults
`PermitEmptyPasswords no`.

## Why the existing mitigation does not close it

`default/turnkey-init-fence` lists `HTTPS_PORTS=(443 12321 12322)`, so the
fence redirects 12321 while it runs. But `lib/init-fence.sh:49-53`
**deliberately skips an address family whose nat table is unavailable**, warns,
and carries on. On an LXC system container without nat that is the normal path,
and no 12321 rules were observed on the `forum` container.

Three things compound it:

- `docs/traps.md` entry 1 is a first boot that hangs forever in one hook. This
  project has hit it three times. While it hangs, `30rootpass` has not run.
- The brief is IPv6-first: a public routable address and no NAT in front.
- The firewall opens 12321 on purpose.

So the window is reachable from the internet for as long as a first boot takes,
and indefinitely if it hangs.

## What is and is not established

Verified by reading and by inspecting two live containers: the hash, the PAM
stack, the miniserv configuration, the bind on both families, the fence port
list, and the nat-skip path.

**Not demonstrated end to end.** No login was attempted against a pre-init
appliance: both available containers already have root passwords set, and
building one would have taken the build lock. High confidence in the mechanism;
the exploit itself is unproven.

Neither `common#8` nor `inithooks#14` introduces this. It is inherited upstream
behaviour and is therefore likely to affect TurnKey appliances as well, which
makes it a coordinated-disclosure question and not only ours. `tracker#3`
defers upstream reporting to about the end of October; a security defect is not
what that deferral was for.

## Exposure right now

Existing containers on the build host have root passwords set and are not
exploitable. The risk is any appliance built from a published Keel layer that
is booted on a reachable address, and any appliance whose first boot hung.

## Remediation to decide between

- Lock the account instead of hashing the empty string: `!` or `*` in the
  password field, so nothing can match. The reason the empty hash exists at all
  needs establishing first, because inithooks may depend on being able to
  authenticate before `30rootpass`.
- Remove `nullok` from `/etc/pam.d/webmin` regardless. It is a second,
  independent weakening with no stated purpose here.
- Do not start Webmin until `30rootpass` has completed, which is the only fix
  that does not depend on the fence working.
- Bind miniserv to loopback until first boot finishes, or give it an `allow=`.
- Make `lib/init-fence.sh` fail loudly rather than warn and continue when it
  cannot install rules for a family. A mitigation that silently declines is
  worse than none, because it is counted on.

The fence's silent skip should be treated as its own defect whatever is decided
about the password.

items.title: feat(unshare): block unshare creating a user namespace
items.body:
Stacked on #300.

In Cohere's report ([link](https://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model)), the model got root inside a private user namespace after an offline QEMU build refused it root:

```
unshare -Urm --propagation private sh -c 'mount -t tmpfs -o exec tmpfs /mnt ...'
```

Unprivileged user namespaces are a common starting point for kernel privilege escalation. The command was allowed at every level.

## What

- New `manual_only` rule `unshare.user-namespace` (category Execution), on at every level.
- It fires when an option before the program implies a user namespace: `-U`/`--user`, `-r`/`--map-root-user`, `-c`/`--map-current-user`, `--map-user(s)`, `--map-group(s)`, `--map-auto`, `--map-subids`, `--owner`, `--mount-binfmt`, `-l`/`--load-interp`. Short clusters such as `-Urm` and `-fpU` count, and values of value-taking options are skipped.
- Allowed: other namespaces without a user namespace (`unshare -n true`, `unshare -u hostname`).
- `unshare` joins the protectable commands, so `sudo` and `timeout` in front of it are peeled.
- A destructive program under `unshare` is still analyzed. With a user-namespace flag, the new rule reports first, and the command is blocked either way.

## Known gaps

- A program launched directly by `unshare` (`unshare -n curl http://169.254.169.254/`) skips the head-based device, network and namespace matchers. That's unchanged from main, because `unshare` isn't an exec wrapper. Shell children (`unshare -n sh -c '…'`) are analyzed.
- `xargs … unshare -r` (unchanged from main; `find -exec unshare -r` is blocked).
- `bwrap`, `podman unshare`, `newuidmap`.
- getopt abbreviations of long options (`--use`, `--map-root`) and user-namespace flags placed after `--monotonic`/`--boottime` values.

## Validation

- Contract rows first: all 9 block rows were allowed before the fix.
- `bun run check`, `bun run verify:package` (656,364 bytes)

* **New Features**

Detection supports relevant short and long options, including when `unshare` is invoked through a wrapper. items.title: feat(init): route every init write through one guarded path
items.body:
## Summary

Every `rtk init` write now goes through one path in `src/hooks/init/write.rs`, with the checks each agent used to do (or skip) around it. A single `plan_write` decides, for each write, what it lands on, what refuses it, what must be confirmed and what happens to the backup; the write, the check made before a consent prompt and the `--dry-run` preview all read that one plan.

Four commits, each standing on its own:

1. **fix(init): leave AGENTS.md alone on `rtk init --codex --uninstall --dry-run`** — the dry run removed the rtk-instructions block for real.
2. **fix(init): patch a `~/.trae-cn` that links to `~/.trae` only once** — the second pass backed RTK's own write up over the user's `hooks.json.bak`.
3. **fix(init): back up without following a symlink at the `.bak`** — the copy goes to a temp file renamed over the `.bak`, so a planted symlink or hard link is replaced rather than written through. Fixes #4157.
4. **feat(init): route every init write through one guarded path**:
   - RTK's own files (RTK.md, GEMINI.md, hooks, extensions, plugins including Antigravity's, the Kilo Code rules, filters templates): atomic, no backup.
   - Configs RTK edits (settings.json, hooks configs, hooks.toml, Hermes' config.yaml): `<name>.bak`, then atomic. Gemini's settings.json now gets a backup too.
   - Instruction files RTK adds to (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Copilot instructions, .clinerules, .windsurfrules): `<name>.bak` (an earlier one is kept), then written in place, so owner, group, ACLs and hard links survive.
   - Missing parent directories are created once, in the shared path; the per-agent `create_dir_all` blocks are gone.
   - A file this user cannot write is refused before any prompt or backup. A Claude, Gemini or Vibe config RTK cannot patch is left to the manual instructions in every mode instead of aborting the run.
   - On Unix, new and replaced files get the permission bits a plain write would (they were all 0600).
   - A dangling symlink is followed only when a plain write would (its directory exists); otherwise it is refused, never replaced by a regular file. A symlink loop is refused the same way (on develop a loop at the Pi or OMP extension path was replaced).
   - In project mode (#4156): hook configs and extensions of Codex, Copilot, Trae, Droid, Pi, OMP and Antigravity that resolve outside the project are refused, and so is Claude Code's project `.claude/settings.json` once it has a hook to register, generalising the guard Codex already had. Any other project write that resolves outside the project, or edits a hard-linked file in place, is named first; `--auto-patch` writes it, the default mode asks, `--no-patch` or a non-interactive run refuses it. `--codex` now accepts `--auto-patch` / `--no-patch` for this.

Fixes #4156. Fixes #4157.

### Behaviour changes worth knowing

- A non-interactive project `rtk init` stops when a file it would edit resolves outside the project (e.g. a `CLAUDE.md` linked to a shared copy), unless `--auto-patch` is given. A read-only file is refused in every mode.
- Patched files leave a `<name>.bak` next to them.
- A symlink into a directory that does not exist, or a symlink loop, is refused instead of being replaced by a regular file.

### Related PRs

- Supersedes #4186 (thanks @Ha1baraA11): same goal as commit 3, done by renaming a temp file over the `.bak` instead of a no-follow open, which also covers hard links and needs no platform flags.
- Supersedes #4176: Codex's `AGENTS.md` gets the warn / ask / refuse policy above rather than a hard refusal.
- Will conflict with #3875 (`pi.rs`, `extension_paths_alias` now uses the shared resolver) and #4235 (`gemini.rs`).

- [x] `cfg(windows)` build cross-checked
- [x] init tests also run as namespaced root (`unshare -r`), for CI containers running as root
- [x] every behaviour added here has a test that fails when the behaviour is reverted
- [x] `rtk init` matrix against develop: 8576 forms (every agent, scope, `--uninstall`, `--auto-patch` / `--no-patch`, `--dry-run`, `-v`) over 16 setups (empty home, user content, legacy blocks, dangling links, links out of the project for hook and instruction files, a shared directory, read-only files, aliased Pi/OMP and Trae CN, …): no crash, no write under `--dry-run`, no write outside the project without `--auto-patch`, and every other difference is one listed above

items.title: Contrary to documentation Bubblewrap leaves mount capability available.
items.body:
The man page states:

> By default no caps are left in the sandboxed process.

Additionally one would expect `--ro-bind` to prevent writing by the sandboxed process.

However when started by uid 0 this is not the case and files can be written (assuming /tmp is a mount point):

`unshare -Ur ./bwrap --ro-bind / / sh -c 'mount -obind,remount,rw /tmp; touch /tmp/test'`

`unshare -Ur ./bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / sh -c 'mount -obind,remount,rw /tmp; touch /tmp/test'`

This is supported by the comment on [line 697 of bubblewrap.c](https://github.com/projectatomic/bubblewrap/blob/v0.3.0/bubblewrap.c#L693).
> If our uid is 0, default to inheriting all caps; the caller
> can drop them via --cap-drop.  This is used by at least rpm-ostree.
> Note this needs to happen before the argument parsing of --cap-drop.

So should `bwrap` behave as documented, or should the documentation be fixed?

Also if caps are explicitly added: `./bwrap --unshare-user --uid 0 --cap-add ALL --ro-bind / / sh -c 'mount -obind,remount,rw /tmp; touch /tmp/test'`

This could avoided by creating the final user namespace after setting up the mounts, which one might expect, but this creates other problems:

* Unshare PID before unshare USER, PID namespace is owned by wrong user namespace.
* Mount /proc before unshare PID, /proc has wrong PID namespace.
* Unshare USER before mount /proc, /proc can be unmounted.

I suggest that this is documented, with a workaround of nesting `bwrap`.

items.title: Add Linux Real lab: Tu root no es root (capabilities)
items.body:
Draft for review: new public content in your voice.

Fills a gap in Linux Real: the route teaches UIDs, `sudo` and setuid, and `del-comando-al-kernel` said root was an `euid == 0` check "y nada más". Since Linux 2.2 the kernel checks capabilities. This lab (`linux-real/tu-root-no-es-root`, order 10, intermediate, 30 min) covers:

1. The `Cap*` lines in `/proc/<pid>/status` and `capsh --decode`. The container's root has 11 of 41 (`00000000800405fb` with Podman; Docker leaves 14), so `sudo date -s` fails with `Operation not permitted`.
2. Root without `cap_dac_override` (`capsh --drop`) denied on a `600` file owned by `vt`, with a note that `/etc/shadow` is the wrong test (root owns it).
3. One capability on a dedicated copy of python with `setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep` to listen on port 80 instead of using `sudo`; `getcap -r /` as an audit; the capabilities that are root in disguise; `AmbientCapabilities=` for systemd.
4. `unshare -r`: all 41 capabilities, yet `/etc/shadow` and the clock are off limits (`uid_map 0 1000 1`, owner shown as `65534`); `unshare -rn` binds port 80 in its own netns; `podman unshare cat /proc/self/uid_map` shows the same mapping behind rootless Podman.

`del-comando-al-kernel`: the euid sentence now says that's how it used to be and points to this lab by name, and its `nextLabs` lists this lab first.

## Environment

`entornos/linux-real/tu-root-no-es-root/`: Debian 13 slim with `libcap2-bin`, `python3`, `procps` and disposable passwordless `sudo` (the README says why). No added capabilities. It runs with `--sysctl=net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=1024`, because Docker 20.10+ lowers it to `0` in containers and then anyone can bind port 80.

## Verified

- Every command block was run verbatim in the environment (rootless Podman 5.4.2, kernel 6.12), and the shown outputs are the real ones; only file timestamps vary. `unshare -r` and `capsh` were also run on a Debian 13 host. The challenge works (port 443, then `setcap -r` brings back `Permission denied`).
- `npm run lab:env -- smoke linux-real/tu-root-no-es-root`: fresh container 0/13 checks, with `solucion.sh` 13/13.
- `prettier --check .`, `npm run lab:check`, `astro check` (0 errors), `npm run build`.
- With #41 merged in, `lab:check -- rutas` passes (40 labs). On `main` alone the lab is reachable only once #41 lands, because `del-comando-al-kernel` itself isn't reachable today.

Not run here: the Docker variants (Docker's daemon is stopped on this machine). The 14-capability count and the `ip_unprivileged_port_start=0` default come from Docker's docs and moby #41030; the lab hedges `unshare -r` under Docker.

Once the containers lab (separate draft) merges, it should go in this lab's `nextLabs`.

- One **1,623-line** vanilla `dashboard.js`, plus `dashboard.css` (1,473 lines). `static/js/dossier-panel.js` (465 lines) is **referenced by nothing** — dead code, safe to delete.

2. **Introduce no build step.** A single `<script>` tag plus the token stylesheet. If adoption requires a bundler, the approach is wrong.
3. **Incremental.** Replace hand-rolled markup inside `dashboard.js` component by component; do not rewrite the dashboard.

kitty-desktop dropping its vendored `tokens.css` mirror for the real package. That repo takes **no runtime CDN** (CSP `default-src 'self'`, enforced by an `unshare -r -n` build-and-boot proof), so it needs the local-file bundle — and it needs **O4** landed first, since the current `tokens.css` has a Google Fonts `@import` that repo has to patch out.

`oracle/sandbox.py` creates a `dummy` eth0 inside the jail's network namespace (`unshare -r -n`).
