items.title: fix(skill): pass module parameters to insmod intact
items.body:
## Summary

`src/os-skills/devops/kernel-dev/scripts/test-module.sh` joined its parameter
arguments into a string (`MODULE_PARAMS="$*"`) and re-expanded that string
**unquoted** into `insmod`, so the shell split a value holding spaces into
several parameters and glob-expanded a value holding `*`, `?` or `[]` against
the current directory before `insmod` ever saw it. Under `set -e` the corrupted
load aborts the suite right after `Loading with parameters: ...`, with no
cleanup — and the kernel rejects the split fragment as an unknown parameter.

The fix keeps the parameters in a bash array and expands it quoted
(`"${MODULE_PARAMS[@]}"`), so each argument reaches `insmod` as exactly one
unmodified parameter. A display-only `MODULE_PARAMS_TEXT` still backs the
`Params:` and `Loading with parameters:` lines, the no-parameter load path is
unchanged, and the usage header plus `examples/README.md` now document the
quoting a value with spaces or glob characters needs.

Before / after, same invocation `test-module.sh param_module 'greeting=Hello World' repeat_count=3 'pattern=*'`
run from a cwd holding `glob-marker` and `pattern=glob-marker`, with the kernel
tools stubbed:

| argv `insmod` receives | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parameters | `greeting=Hello`, `World`, `repeat_count=3`, `pattern=glob-marker` | `greeting=Hello World`, `repeat_count=3`, `pattern=*` |
| suite exit code | non-zero (aborts at step 3) | 0, `Test Complete!` |

`shellcheck` independently flagged the old expansion (`SC2086` on the `insmod`
line); the fixed script reports no findings at any severity.

## Related issue

Fixes #3744

## Testing

Environment: Linux x86_64, GNU bash 4.4.20, Python 3.8.17, pytest 8.3.5,
ShellCheck 0.10.0. No kernel, no real module, no root account and no network are
needed — `unshare -r` satisfies the script's `EUID == 0` check and stubbed
`insmod`/`lsmod`/`rmmod`/`modinfo`/`dmesg`/`sleep` binaries are placed first on
`PATH`; the stub `insmod` records the argv it receives.

New regression test `tests/os-skills/test_kernel_dev_module_params.py` (3 cases:
value with a space, value with glob characters, no parameters at all). It runs
the real script from a temporary copy of the skill layout, so the repository tree
is untouched.

Red → green, both with `unshare -r` and with the test's root-check-neutralised
fallback (the path CI containers without user namespaces take):

```
$ git stash push src/os-skills/devops/kernel-dev/scripts/test-module.sh   # main version
$ python3 -m pytest tests/os-skills/test_kernel_dev_module_params.py -q
2 failed, 1 passed        # space case: ['greeting=Hello', 'World', ...]
                          # glob case:  ['pattern=glob-marker', ...]
$ git stash pop
$ python3 -m pytest tests/os-skills/test_kernel_dev_module_params.py -q
3 passed
```

Everything else that was run:

```
$ bash -n src/os-skills/devops/kernel-dev/scripts/test-module.sh      # no output, exit 0
$ shellcheck src/os-skills/devops/kernel-dev/scripts/test-module.sh   # no findings (main: SC2086)
$ python3 -m pytest tests/os-skills/ -q                               # 12 passed
      (6 pdf-reader tables + 3 skill-usage + 3 new)
$ bash scripts/docs-lint.sh                                           # naming + en/zh parity OK
$ python3 scripts/docs-link-check.py                                  # all relative links resolve
$ make -C src/os-skills build                                         # informational only: os-skills has no build step
```

Manual end-to-end run of the fixed script under `unshare -r` with the stubs:

```
Params: greeting=Hello World repeat_count=3 pattern=*
Loading with parameters: greeting=Hello World repeat_count=3 pattern=*
insmod argv: [<...>/param_module.ko] [greeting=Hello World] [repeat_count=3] [pattern=*]
Test Complete!        (exit 0)
```

Not run, with reasons:

- Loading a real kernel module (`param_module.ko` built from `examples/`) on a
  running kernel: the sandbox has no root outside a user namespace, no kernel
  build tree and no module loading permitted, so the acceptance criteria were
  verified against a stub `insmod` that records argv — the layer where the defect
  lives (argument construction), not the kernel's parameter parser.
- `tests/run-all-tests.sh --filter`: it has no `os-skills` filter, so the
  component's tests were run directly with pytest as above.

## Risk and compatibility

Behaviour changes only for parameter arguments that the shell used to mangle —
values with spaces, tabs or glob characters — which previously produced a failed
`insmod` and an aborted suite. Simple `name=value` parameters take the same code
path and are passed unchanged; the no-parameter invocation is untouched. The
script remains bash-only (`#!/bin/bash`, array syntax) as before, and no skill
directory was added, removed or renamed, so `component.toml` and
`os-skills.spec.in` need no update. Rollback is a single-commit revert.

items.title: fix(linux): trust GNOME Shell and KWin after an update replaced their binary
items.body:
## Problem

On kdesk (Fedora 44, GNOME 50) `gnome-shell` 50.6 was installed at 09:36 while the 08:34 session kept running. `/proc/<pid>/exe` then read `/usr/bin/gnome-shell (deleted)` and `stat()` on that path failed, so `is_trusted_gnome_shell` refused the real Shell. Reproduced against the deployed fdd82a139 service:

- `list_windows`: all 8 windows from the AT-SPI fallback (pid-based ids, no `helper_epoch`, no `capture_current`), although the WinRects helper answered `GetCapabilities` (protocol 4) and `GetVersion` (14) on the Shell's own connection.
- `get_window_state` on a visible window: `refused` / `stale_snapshot`.

So computer use stayed broken until the user logged out. KWin's trust check had the same shape.

## Fix

`proc_fs::running_executable(pid)` reads the link and stats the running image through `/proc/<pid>/exe` (following the magic link reaches the inode even once unlinked), and drops the kernel's ` (deleted)` suffix only when that image has no links left. `is_trusted_gnome_shell` and `is_trusted_kwin` apply the unchanged rule (file name, root-owned, not group/other writable) to the running inode instead of the file now at the path. That is at least as strict on an un-updated system. KWin's `read_link failed => true` branch is preserved.

## Evidence (kdesk, contained env)

- fmt, release build, `platform-linux` 10/10 parallel runs (864 passed each), `--features portal-input` 2/2 (885), `cua-driver --features portal-input` (446), `cua-driver-contract` (72).
- New tests: a real copy of `sleep` named `gnome-shell`, run and then unlinked. Under `unshare -r` (files show as root-owned) the replaced Shell is trusted; as a normal user it is not. Mutations: restoring the old path-based Shell check fails the Shell test under `unshare -r`; keeping the ` (deleted)` suffix fails both tests in both modes.
- The first round's new test hit `ETXTBSY` once in three runs (a child forked by a parallel test held the copy's write descriptor until its exec); it now retries briefly, and 10/10 parallel runs pass.
- Memcheck base-versus-candidate: see the PR comment.

items.title: Rootless Podman Compatibility
items.body:
`vagrant up` as [recommended](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/development/setup-recommended.html) doesn't work with `podman-docker` because podman runs rootless by default, and the Vagrantfile volume-mounts the repo directory into the container _assuming that UID `${UID}` on the container will also be UID ${UID} on the host_, which is true under rootful docker but not rootless podman (and probably not under rootless docker either though I haven't tested that). Permissions get janky. 

## Other Solutions

* `sudo vagrant up`  doesn't work because then vagrant is running as root and the `VAGRANT_UID=#{Process.uid}` line causes it to try to `useradd -u 0 vagrant` within the container, which isn't allowed
  * but it **does** work if the Vagrantfile hardcodes `VAGRANT_UID=1000` (or whatever your user ID is) 
  * or in theory if it examined `${SUDO_UID}` instead I guess
  * annoying because you have to `sudo vagrant ssh` to access the container
* You can make one of the mapped groups into a project group shared with the container

    ```
    mkdir -p .vagrant;
    chmod -R g+w .
    sudo groupadd -g 100999 -U $USER vagrant-podman
    podman unshare chown -R 1000:1000 .
    podman unshare chown -R 0:0 .vagrant
    vagrant up --provider=docker
    ```

    Though this will lead to some files being owned by the container user and some being owned by.

## This Solution

podman by default maps host $UID to container root and any other container uid N to host UID 100000+n (well, for the first account; details in /etc/subuid).

This solution uses a podman-specifc [--uidmap](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-create.1.html#uidmap-flags-container-uid-from-uid-amount) flag to rearrange that mapping.

Instead of root <=> ${UID}, container ${UID} <=> 100999, we this makes ${UID} <=> ${UID} and it pushes container root <=> 199999. Um. Which is a bit weird? Couldn't we just swap the two? Whatever this works.

  (and don't worry it's okay, podman can still become container root because the UID it uses for container root is still one of your _subordinate_ UIDs)

Pay close attention to the note in the docs:

> In the rootless case, host UIDs are not mapped directly to container UIDs. Instead the mapping happens over two mapping steps:
>
> host UID -> intermediate UID -> container UID
>
> The --uidmap option only influences the second mapping step.
>
> The first mapping step is derived by Podman from the contents of the file /etc/subuid and the UID of the user calling Podman.

Developed in [#development help > rootless podman @ 💬](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/rootless.20podman/near/2409791)

items.title: security: the bare tier's children run at subordinate host ids, or the tier stays insecure (Program C, C2)
items.body:
Program C, phase **C2**: the bare tier separates its children for real, or it stays the C0 insecure mode. It is never claimed separated when it isn't.

> **Stacked on #3478 (C0b).** This branch contains C0b's three commits. Once #3478 merges, this PR is rebased onto main so that only the C2 commit remains.

## Why

An unprivileged user namespace that maps the child back to the node's own host uid isolates nothing, because file access is checked against host credentials. On main, every bare-tier child (`/v1/run`, the workload, and the companion) runs at the node's uid. Each one can read the 0700 state directory and `state/ca/ca-key.pem`.

## What

**1. Subordinate host ids (`crates/nucleus/src/hardening/{subordinate,userns}.rs`).**

A new posture, `Posture::Subordinate(SubordinateIds)`, is reached only from `Unsandboxed` on a non-root runtime with `UnsandboxedOptIn::Subordinate(ids)`. Between fork and exec, the hook does this:

- sweeps inherited fds;
- forks two helpers (before the namespace exists), runs `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`, then lets the helpers exec the setuid `newuidmap` / `newgidmap`, each with exactly `id id 1`. Both helpers must exit 0;
- drops supplementary groups, then calls `setresgid` and `setresuid` to the subordinate ids;
- clears ambient capabilities;
- reads `/proc/self/{uid,gid}_map` back and refuses to exec unless each is exactly `id id 1`. The `unshare -r` shape `0 <node uid> 1` is refused;
- sets `no_new_privs`, the rlimits and the Landlock write layer, then installs the **workload denylist + derived classes**. That filter refuses nested `CLONE_NEWUSER`.

No new `unsafe`: the steps use rustix safe wrappers, and only `fork` / `execve` / `_exit` / `unshare` / `prctl` sit in the existing audited block. The exemplar `unsafe_blocks` count stays at 8.

On the node side:

- Each pod gets its own ids from the node user's delegated range. The offset is persisted in `state/subordinate-ids.next` and an id is never reused.
- The proxy re-validates the delegation of `--subordinate-ids` itself, and refuses to start rather than run its children at its own uid.
- A companion with its own explicit uid is refused.

**2. Realization contract, one decider (`nucleus::LocalRealization::check`).** It has four clauses:

| Clause | How it is checked |
|---|---|
| Signing material unreachable | The child's host uid is neither the node's nor 0, and the state dir is 0700 with no access ACL. A probe child, spawned through the **real hook**, must fail to `cd` into the state dir. |
| No impersonate / signal / ptrace | Distinct host uid, so `SO_PEERCRED` names the subordinate uid. The probe must fail to `kill -0` the node. |
| Protected effects stay mediated | The workload denylist and the pod's derived classes. |
| Holds across child creation | Nested namespaces are refused, and `no_new_privs` stops setuid helpers. |

If the contract is **met**, the node runs as `EvidenceTier::SeparatedLocal`:

- claims and pod receipts state `separated-local`;
- claims are signed with the executor key and pod receipts with the cert root;
- `verify_execution` refuses `separated-local` as `NotProtectedMicroVm`, even when it is paired with `backend = firecracker`;
- trusted authorities are still refused. Lifting that is a separate decision.

If the contract is **unmet**, the node stays in C0 insecure mode, unchanged, and logs the failed clause.

**3. `proxy.sock` peer auth.** A new flag, `--node-peer-pid`, admits the node's own process alone, and only while it is still the proxy's parent. A recycled pid admits nobody. This is the `ArmContainerInit` pid pattern. It replaces the uid-only `PodPeer` admission on the local driver, in both the separated and the insecure mode.

**4. Operator identity (`--operator-identity-dir`).** The node mints the `--root-minter-spiffe-id` client certificate into a 0700 directory outside the state directory. Both cross-pod gates now use it and no longer read `state/ca/ca-key.pem`. Their verdict logic is unchanged.

**5. Workspace grant.** The node grants the workspace by POSIX ACL only when `work_dir` is strictly inside a `--workspace-root` that lies outside the state dir and does not overlap another pod's workspace. In that case the workload door moves into the workspace. No path a creator names is ever widened.

**6. CI images.** `uidmap` is installed, and `usermod --add-subuids/--add-subgids 200000-265535 runner` is run in `docker/Dockerfile.runner` and `ci/fly-runner/Dockerfile`. Docs: `docs/bare-tier-insecure.md` (separated vs insecure, plus operator setup).

## Evidence (builder `nucleus-agent-build`, Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, non-root user `bcrisp`, subuid `165536:65536`)

**Canary through the actual `spawn_admitted`** (`workload::subordinate_canary_tests`). The canary is `state/ca/ca-key.pem` at 0600 in a 0700 `ca/` dir in a 0700 state dir:

- Shared-uid control (main's behaviour): the canary is read.
- Separated: the child reports `id -u = 165547`, the read fails with `Permission denied`, and the secret is absent.

**End to end on a real local-driver node** (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`). The workload of pod A ran with:

```
out.txt: 165537 kill=1 done
leaked.txt bytes: 0
denied.txt: cat: …/state/ca/ca-key.pem: Permission denied
ls_state.txt: ls: cannot open directory '…/state': Permission denied
kill.txt: kill: Operation not permitted
proxy args: --node-peer-pid 322357 --subordinate-ids 165537:165537 (pod B: 165538:165538)
```

**Cross-pod `proxy.sock`.** A node-uid process that is not the node connects to pod B's `proxy.sock`: `curl` exits 56 (closed at accept). The node's own path still serves. Unit tests cover the same case: `a_same_uid_process_that_is_not_the_node_is_refused_at_accept`, plus a control showing the uid rule served it.

**Fail-closed** (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, Ubuntu's default):

- The probe fails with `Operation not permitted` and the node starts in insecure mode: marker, insecure key, canary readable, as in C0.
- The live gates still pass.
- With `NUCLEUS_REQUIRE_SUBORDINATE_IDS=1`, the canary test reds: `contract is unmet: … spawn: Operation not permitted`.

**Live gates** run as a non-root user, both modes: `cross-pod-lineage-check.sh` OK and `cross-pod-scoped-check.sh` OK, using the node-minted operator identity.

**Builder checks:**

- clippy `-D warnings --all-targets --all-features` for nucleus, nucleus-tool-proxy (plus `--features spire`), nucleus-node and nucleus-ci-verdict: clean.
- nextest for the same crates (with `NUCLEUS_REQUIRE_SUBORDINATE_IDS=1`): 2172/2172 pass.
- `xtask prepush`: exemplar, audit, scorecard, line ratchet and fmt pass. "Tests of affected crates" cannot run on the builder, which has no `sdks/verifier-js/pkg` wasm build (environmental; CI builds it).

## Perturbation table (each row red-first on the builder, restored, tree verified clean)

| id | perturbation | caught by | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | map check accepts namespace uid 0 (the `unshare -r` shape) as separated, i.e. the "namespace uid 0 is isolated" mutation | `only_a_one_id_identity_map_of_the_subordinate_id_is_accepted` | RED |
| P2 | subordinate opt-in realized as the shared-uid posture | canary via `spawn_admitted`, live canary, `a_subordinate_opt_in_separates_every_bare_tier_child`, `the_child_runs_at_its_subordinate_ids_with_no_groups` | RED |
| P3 | hook skips `setresuid` (map written, uid unchanged) | canary via `spawn_admitted`, live canary, `the_child_runs_at_its_subordinate_ids…` | RED |
| P4 | hook keeps the node's supplementary groups | `the_child_runs_at_its_subordinate_ids_with_no_groups` | RED |
| P5 | contract accepts a state dir with group/other bits | `a_shared_state_directory_is_not_separated` | RED |
| P6 | `proxy.sock` node binding ignores the peer pid (uid alone) | `the_node_binding_admits_the_node_process_alone`, `a_same_uid_process_that_is_not_the_node_is_refused_at_accept` | RED |
| P7 | a delegated id equal to the runtime uid is accepted | `an_id_that_is_the_runtime_or_root_is_refused` | RED |
| P8 | `verify_execution` accepts `separated-local` as a microVM | `separated_local_evidence_never_passes_as_a_microvm` | RED |
| P9 | workspace grant allows the root itself | `a_grant_is_confined_to_the_workspace_root` | RED |
| P10 | a separated local node claims the driver tier | `a_delegated_host_separates_and_never_reuses_an_id` | RED |
| P11 | the id pool hands out the same id again | `a_delegated_host_separates_and_never_reuses_an_id` | RED |
| P12 | operator identity dir accepted inside the state dir | `the_operator_directory_is_private_and_outside_the_state_directory` | RED |
| P13 | separated children get no syscall filter (nested user namespace possible) | `the_child_cannot_signal_the_node_or_make_a_namespace` | RED |
| G1 | scoped listing filter bypassed (A sees sibling B) | `scripts/cross-pod-scoped-check.sh` | RED |
| G2 | the parent an operator names on create is not recorded | `scripts/cross-pod-lineage-check.sh` | RED |

P1–P4 and P13 were re-run on the final hook code (after the rustix rewrite).

## Guardrail paths touched (advisory)

- `scripts/cross-pod-lineage-check.sh`, `scripts/cross-pod-scoped-check.sh`: operator identity from the node instead of the CA key. Same verdict logic; reds per G1 and G2.
- `ci/fly-runner/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.runner`: `uidmap` and the subordinate range for `runner`.

## Left for the owner

- **Runner images.** The two Dockerfiles change, but the images are built elsewhere. Until they are rebuilt and redeployed, CI's live gates run the insecure fallback, which is still green. After the rebuild, the runner kernel must also allow unprivileged user namespaces with capabilities: Fly's kernel probably does; Ubuntu with `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1` does not. Otherwise the node falls back to insecure, by name. To make CI *prove* separation, set `NUCLEUS_REQUIRE_SUBORDINATE_IDS=1` in the Tests and live-gate jobs (`.github/**`, not touched here).
- **Trusted authorities on `SeparatedLocal`.** They are still refused, so lifting the refusal is your call.
- **Builder sysctl.** I set `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` to 0 on the builder for the separated runs. It is restored to 1 at the end.

## What

257 test call sites in 22 files built inodes with `create_core` / `mkdir_core` / `symlink_core` / `mknod_core` and a hard-coded `1000, 1000` caller. They now use `FsTestExt`:


items.title: OCI workload process runs with NoNewPrivs=0 and a full capability bounding set
items.body:
Narrowed 2026-08-14. The original report bundled two findings; the first was root-caused, corrected twice, and **fixed on `main` by PR #2102 (`343eccce1`)**. This issue now tracks only the second, which was always independent of the kernel question and is unchanged by those corrections.

## The remaining defect

The OCI workload process runs with `NoNewPrivs: 0` and a full capability bounding set (`CapBnd: 000001ffffffffff`) on **both** priority backends.

| Probe | HVF (macOS 26.5.2 arm64) | Firecracker (Linux 6.8, KVM) |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uid=901 gid=901` | `uid=901 gid=901` |
| `CapEff` | `0000000000000000` | `0000000000000000` |
| `CapBnd` | `000001ffffffffff` (full) | `000001ffffffffff` (full) |
| `NoNewPrivs` | `0` | `0` |

ADR-001 names `setpriv --bounding-set=-all --no-new-privs` (W2.3) as a mechanism behind claims 1 and 2, and `set_no_new_privs()` exists in `mvm-seccomp-apply` — but that path and `mvm-setpriv` are wired from the nix-built guest (`nix/flake.nix`, `nix/tests/mk-guest-eval.nix`), not from `mvm-oci-init`. `crates/mvm-agentd/src/bin/mvm-oci-init.rs` contains no `no_new_privs` or bounding-set call at all.

**The outcome today still holds, but by circumstance rather than by the named mechanism.** The image ships zero setuid binaries and the rootfs is read-only, so nothing escalates. With `no_new_privs` off, setuid bits and file capabilities *would* be honoured on exec if an image ever shipped one.

## Scope decision required

Whether ADR-001 claims 1 and 2 are scoped to mkGuest *services* — where W2.3 is applied — or extend to the OCI workload process is an owner call, and it determines whether this is a claim-bearing fix or a defense-in-depth one. Same tier question raised by #2091.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Record the claims 1/2 scope decision.
- [ ] Define the minimal capability set the authenticated activation and restore paths actually require, and apply `no_new_privs` plus that bounding set before workload exec.
- [ ] Test setuid binaries, file capabilities, user-namespace attempts, and syscall failure paths.
- [ ] Re-run the adversarial probe on HVF **and** Firecracker before closure. A probe that reports the starting uid does not close this — the original finding was only visible because the probe *attempted* elevation. Harness: `specs/research/no-root-workload-live-witness.md`.

---

## Withdrawn from the original report

Both were inferences that the built artifacts contradicted. Recorded here so they are not rediscovered as facts.

**1. "`NAMESPACES` is in `requiredExtraDisables` and is being silently overridden."** Wrong mechanism. The built workload kernel config has `CONFIG_NAMESPACES=y` and `# CONFIG_USER_NS is not set`. `CONFIG_USER_NS` is the discriminator, and it has been off in workload kernels independently of Plan 286. There is no evidence `requiredExtraDisables` was ever overridden.

**2. "This is an HVF property."** Wrong cause — it was host cache state. The HVF guest console banner (`root@(none)`) is a byte-exact match for `~/.mvm/cache/default-microvm/prod/vmlinux`, and that Mac had no `~/.mvm/cache/builder-vm/aarch64/kernels/` directory at all. The Firecracker host had a real workload kernel cached; the Mac did not, and the run fell through to the default-microvm kernel, which has `CONFIG_USER_NS=y`. **A Firecracker host without a cached workload kernel would have behaved identically.**

That kernel-selection defect — `ensure_workload_kernel` accepting a default-microVM kernel as a cache hit, so the loud cold-cache error was never reached — is **fixed on `main` by PR #2102**. The workload path now accepts only the dedicated workload kernel, with regression tests for both dev and prod cache layouts.

Original report and probe output: `specs/research/no-root-workload-live-witness.md` (PR #2098). Related: #2091 (same family, found the same way). Tracked through `specs/plans/300-open-issue-closeout.md` Phase 1.

items.title: privilege model: no root refusal, no capability drop, clone/clone3 bypass the namespace filter
items.body:
Two related gaps in the privilege model.

1. Root is not refused. `isolation::enter` maps `{uid} {uid} 1`, so when bailey runs as uid 0 the target is uid 0 on the host: its files are root-owned and DAC stops being a barrier, leaving Landlock as the only one. There is no `geteuid() == 0` guard anywhere in the run path (`isolation.rs`, `enforce.rs`, `cli.rs`). This is not hypothetical: the reference harness records the deployed cage running as uid 0 and flags it in `docs/gap-analysis.md`. The documented model is unprivileged; bailey should refuse to run as root, or refuse the `0 0 1` mapping, rather than silently produce a root process.

2. No capabilities are dropped and the namespace filter is bypassable. After `isolation::enter` the target keeps the full capability set of its user namespace, and nothing clears the bounding set, ambient set or securebits before `execve`. `denied_syscalls` names `unshare` and `setns` but not `clone` or `clone3`, so `clone(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWNET|...)` is reachable. That defeats the stated intent of those two denials.

   The practical impact is bounded today: the target is already root in its user
   namespace, and `mount`, `fsopen`, `open_tree`, `move_mount`, `mount_setattr`
   are all denied, so a new namespace adds no reach against resources owned by
   the parent namespace. It stops being bounded the moment (a) capabilities are
   dropped later and a nested user namespace restores them for the child, or
   (b) any future right or syscall assumes "the target cannot create a
   namespace". `clone3` cannot be argument-filtered by seccomp at all (the flags
   are behind a pointer), so filtering only `clone` leaves the bypass open.

Fix, in order of value:

- refuse to run as root;
- after the namespaces are built and before `execve`, drop every capability (`capset` to empty), clear the ambient set, and set the securebits that stop the kernel from re-granting caps on `setuid`/`exec` (`SECBIT_NOROOT | SECBIT_NOROOT_LOCKED | SECBIT_NO_SETUID_FIXUP...` as appropriate). A target without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` in its user namespace cannot create `NEWNS`/`NEWPID`/`NEWUTS`/`NEWNET` through any clone variant, which is the robust fix for the syscall gap;
- if a seccomp rule is still wanted, deny `clone3` (glibc falls back to `clone` only on `ENOSYS`, so a denial must be tested against threading) or inspect it with a seccomp user-notification supervisor.

items.title: test: guard permission tests once, run CI as root, crash-test the binary
items.body:
## Why

Some tests only passed on the machine they were written on. Under root, the `chmod` tests broke, because root ignores file permissions. Under a non-English locale, two tests that match git's English messages broke. Against a compiled binary, the killed-sync tests skipped, so crash recovery was never tested on the shipped build.

## What changed

items.title: Refuse to run the sim harness outside an isolated PID namespace
items.body:
On 2026-10-21 a Swift test on the Mac started the Python sim harness outside the safe namespace. On ovh, an earlier code-job `kill_tree()` with a root of 0, 1 or empty signalled every `ubuntu` process. With this PR the harness, the code-job stub tests and the signal-sending tests refuse to run unless they are isolated. Design: `sim/ISOLATION.md`.

## Linux
- `sim/sim_isolation.py` is the first import of every `sim/*.py` (66 modules). A lint test checks that it stays first. Outside isolation it exits 78 and names `sudo -u sbtest -- unshare -r -p -f --mount-proc ...`.
- Isolation is decided from `/proc` alone. All three must hold:
  - the process is not in the initial pidns (`pid:[4026531836]`);
  - `/proc/self` equals `getpid()`, which proves `--mount-proc`;
  - pid 1 of the namespace is in the same namespace and is an ancestor of the process.
- No environment variable can claim isolation. When the launcher looks like a Swift/XCTest run, the refusal says so.
- `code-job-test.sh`, `bot-msg-test.sh` and `mac-codex-tmp-smoke.sh` run `/usr/bin/python3 -I -B sim/sim_isolation.py --check` before anything else. The interpreter path is absolute, so a stub `python3` on PATH cannot answer the check.

## macOS: signal-guarded mode
macOS has no pidns, so the harness runs only with a signal guard. The Swift tests still exercise the real shipped scripts.
- The guard wraps `os.kill`, `os.killpg` and `signal.pidfd_send_signal`. The first two also cover `Popen.send_signal`, `terminate` and `kill`.
- It refuses:
  - targets <= 1, except the process itself;
  - negative, non-int or empty targets;
  - its own group when it does not lead it;
  - anything it did not spawn (Popen, fork, posix_spawn, multiprocessing), directly or through its children;
  - a reaped child's pid, which may since have been reused.
- Signal 0 (an existence probe) may still name any pid above 1.
- The same guard also runs inside the Linux namespace.
- `live_observed --offline` reports the mode, and `ObservedPatternTests` requires `"darwin-guarded"`.

## Defence in depth
- `swarm_lifecycle` never calls `killpg()` on a group that is not `private_group()`: <= 1, non-int, or its own group.
- The pid-file kills in `code-job-test.sh` go through `own_pid`.
- code-job `kill_tree`, `swarm_store.terminate` and the verifiers were already guarded in 199f68f.

## Tests (Linux, all as `sudo -u sbtest -- unshare -r -p -f --mount-proc`, at 89ffe17)
| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `discover -s Tests/Updater` | 247 OK (1 skipped) |
| `discover -s scripts` | 661 OK (1 skipped) |
| `discover -s sim` | 642 run; the same 6 failures + 7 errors as origin/main 1d7a3bb (603 run), 0 new |
| `code-job-test.sh` sh / dash | 24/24, 24/24 |
| `bot-msg-test.sh` sh / dash | 14/14, 14/14 |

The new tests are `sim/test_sim_isolation.py` (32) and `sim/test_signal_guards.py` (7). They cover:
- refusal outside the namespace: a synthetic `/proc`, plus a real nested pidns without its own `/proc`;
- a Swift-style `live_observed.py` launch, which is refused before it writes anything and starts inside the namespace;
- refusal of bad pids and groups, with recorders standing in for real signals;
- real signals sent only to the test's own children.

A mutation check made the guards return "OK" and turned 15 tests red.

Not run: macOS. A Mac verification run is scheduled separately.

items.title: Case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing volumes reinstate the refresh-staging sweep's self-delete for a case- or NFC-variant planned dest
items.body:
<!-- neutral-deferred-finding: pr#2489 feedea0800a0800af42cea1840a668f1da278a6e finding:4 -->

Source: #2489 at feedea0800a0800af42cea1840a668f1da278a6e
Location: src/core/runtime/client_assets.js:788
Severity: minor

## Evidence
The guard planned.some((entry) => entry.dest === stage) is byte equality, but statShape (client_assets.js:674) uses fs.stat, which resolves names under the volume's identity rules, and isSafeContributionName (src/core/runtime/contribution_names.js) applies no case or Unicode folding, so demo.HYP-REFRESH is a legal contribution name. On a case-insensitive volume (APFS and NTFS defaults; the release checklist mandates a manual macOS host), installing demo derives stage <skills>/demo.hyp-refresh, fs.stat resolves it onto the freshly installed demo.HYP-REFRESH, the byte comparison is false, and fs.rm then deletes the copy this same run made and reported installed, on every run, while the ledger goes on naming it. That is round 1 finding 1 restored for a case-variant name: a destructive behavior this PR introduces on supported platforms. Mechanism verified in source at feedea08; not executable in this container or on CI (ubuntu-latest for all three jobs, case-sensitive container, no root, loop device, or mkfs).

## Expected behavior
A contribution this run installed is never swept by its own neighbour under the volume's own name-identity relation, the same invariant c43e26cb established for byte-identical names: demo.HYP-REFRESH keeps its own body across repeated installs on a case-insensitive volume, and no 'removed leftover refresh staging' line or client_assets.refresh_staging_removed event names it.

## Why deferral is safe
Safe to defer rather than block: reachability is adversarial-third-party only (a plugin must register, for one client, both X and a case- or normalization-variant of X.hyp-refresh, mimicking an internal reserved staging suffix; no bundled contribution is anything close), the delete stays at a derived direct child of the asset directory (no containment escape) and destroys only the plugin's own freshly copied contribution, never user-authored content, and the candidate repairs carry a real design trade: naive case-fold plus NFC widening declines genuine leftovers whenever the plan holds a case-variant, which is issue 2407's own symptom in an equally contrived case but in the non-destructive direction, while true file identity (dev/ino) is unavailable for plan entries not yet copied. Blocking would hold a real recovery fix hostage to an adversarial name on platforms this repository's CI cannot exercise.

## Acceptance condition
Two parts, each testable. (1) Deterministic on existing ubuntu CI: a regression test that fails at feedea08 and passes after the repair, pinning the repair's comparison semantics for a case-fold or NFC-variant planned dest; for example, with a widened comparison, a genuine leftover at demo.hyp-refresh is declined, not removed, when the plan contains demo.HYP-REFRESH on a case-sensitive volume. (2) End-to-end on a case-insensitive volume: register X and X.HYP-REFRESH for one client, run the installer twice, and assert X.HYP-REFRESH keeps its own body and no removed-leftover line or refresh_staging_removed event names it, in a test that probes its fixture directory for case-insensitivity (create a lowercase probe, fs.stat the uppercase spelling) and reports a skip where the probe fails, exercised on a macos-latest CI leg or the release checklist's mandatory manual macOS gate.

Evidenced behavioral defect; eligible for automatic repair.

items.title: `npm test` on a Wayland session can take over the developer's XWayland display (`linuxInputRegionNative.test.js`)
items.body:
On Linux, `test/helpers/linuxInputRegionNative.test.js` (added in #2161) starts `Xvfb -displayfd 3` and lets Xvfb choose a display number. Xvfb doesn't skip a display that is already in use when that display has no abstract socket. Hyprland's XWayland is set up that way, and it was on `:1`:

- `/tmp/.X1-lock` belongs to the live Hyprland process.
- Hyprland listens on `/tmp/.X11-unix/X1` and `X1_`, with no abstract `@/tmp/.X11-unix/X1`.

So Xvfb picks `:1`, unlinks the live `/tmp/.X11-unix/X1` and binds its own socket there. The test then SIGKILLs Xvfb, which leaves a dead socket file at that path. XWayland keeps running, but nothing can reach `:1` by its normal path any more. Every X11 client in the desktop session gets `Connection refused` until the next login.

For OpenWhispr itself, this means the next launch crashes. The launcher forces `--ozone-platform=x11` on Wayland, Electron fails with:

```
ERROR:ui/ozone/platform/x11/ozone_platform_x11.cc:256] Missing X server or $DISPLAY
ERROR:ui/aura/env.cc:246] The platform failed to initialize.  Exiting.
```

and then it segfaults in `uv_close` while exiting. With systemd-coredump's defaults, each crash wrote a ~32 GB core dump, which kept the disk saturated for about 5 minutes per crash. I lost a few hours to this before tracing it back to the test run.

**To Reproduce**

On a real session:

1. Use Hyprland, with XWayland on `:1`, and Xvfb, gcc and the X11/Xtst/Xext headers installed so the test doesn't skip.
2. Run `npm test` in the repo.
3. Run `DISPLAY=:1 xdpyinfo`. It now fails, and `/tmp/.X11-unix/X1` has the timestamp of the test run.

Without touching a real session: the script below runs inside a private user/mount/network namespace with a fresh `/tmp`. It creates a fake live display `:0` laid out like Hyprland's (path-only sockets plus a lock file held by a live process), then runs Xvfb the way the test does.

```bash
unshare -r -m -n --propagation private bash -c '
mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /tmp; mkdir -m 1777 /tmp/.X11-unix
python3 -c "
import socket,os,time
s=[socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX) for _ in range(2)]
for x,p in zip(s,(\"/tmp/.X11-unix/X0\",\"/tmp/.X11-unix/X0_\")): x.bind(p); x.listen(1)
open(\"/tmp/.X0-lock\",\"w\").write(\"%10d\n\"%os.getpid()); time.sleep(30)" &
sleep 1
Xvfb -displayfd 3 -screen 0 1024x768x24 -nolisten tcp 3>/tmp/display 2>/dev/null & XV=$!
sleep 2; echo "Xvfb chose :$(cat /tmp/display)"; kill -KILL $XV; sleep 0.5
python3 -c "import socket;socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX).connect(\"/tmp/.X11-unix/X0\")" && echo ":0 still reachable" || echo ":0 is broken"
kill %1'
```

Output (trimmed):

```
Xvfb chose :0
ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused
:0 is broken
```

Xvfb took the display even though a live process held the lock and the socket was accepting connections.

**Expected behavior**

Running the test suite shouldn't affect the developer's desktop session. The test should use a display number that is actually free, and leave existing displays alone.

**Possible fix**

Instead of `-displayfd`, choose the display explicitly. Starting from a high number (as `xvfb-run -a` does from 99), skip any `n` where `/tmp/.X<n>-lock` or `/tmp/.X11-unix/X<n>` exists. Then start `Xvfb :<n>`; with an explicit display, Xvfb checks the lock file instead of claiming the display. Shutting it down with SIGTERM instead of SIGKILL would also let Xvfb remove its own socket and lock file.

**Desktop:**

- OS: Arch Linux, kernel 6.18 LTS
- Compositor: Hyprland 0.56.2 (Wayland, XWayland on `:1`)
- Xvfb: xorg-server-xvfb 21.1.24
- OpenWhispr: `upstream/main` at 7a690796; installed app 1.10.2 (Electron 41.10.5)

**Additional context**

- Electron segfaulting instead of exiting cleanly when the X server is unreachable is an Electron problem. electron/electron#54372 covers a related case: no fallback to Wayland when X11 is missing.
- I recovered the display without logging out by symlinking `/tmp/.X11-unix/X1` to Hyprland's still-live `X1_` socket.

---

I'd like to work on the fix and open the PR myself, if that's okay with you. Let me know if the approach above works for you or if you'd prefer something different.

items.title: deep-review: n8-mac-changer — ERR: failed live MAC change leaves the interface administratively DOWN with no rollback
items.body:
**Severity: High** · Layer: ERR · `firmware/mac_changer.py:174-187`

## Summary

`change_mac_linux()` brings the interface **down** first, then sets the new address, then brings it **up**. If the middle step fails, the third step is never reached and there is no `try/finally` / rollback, so the interface is left **administratively down** — the host loses that link permanently until someone manually runs `ip link set <if> up`. `change_mac_osx()` has no down/up step, so this is Linux-specific.

`SECURITY.md` explicitly lists *"broken sandboxing/safety gating"* as a reportable defect class; this is the availability half of it.

## Root cause (`firmware/mac_changer.py:174-187`)

```python
def change_mac_linux(self, interface, new_mac):
    try:
        subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface, 'down'],
                       check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=5)      # <-- link dropped
        subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface,
                        'address', new_mac],
                       check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=5)      # <-- may fail here
        subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface, 'up'],
                       check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=5)      # <-- never runs
        return True
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"[-] Error: {e.stderr.decode() if e.stderr else e}")
        return False
```

There is no state to restore and no `finally` block, so control flow on the failure path is: `down` succeeds → `address` raises → `return False`. The link stays down.

## Reproduction (verified by execution)

Environment: Linux 6.18.54, iproute2-7.2.0, `unshare -r -n` network namespace with a `veth0`/`veth1` pair.

```
$ ip link add veth0 type veth peer name veth1
$ ip link set veth0 up
$ ip -o link show veth0
3: veth0@veth1: <NO-CARRIER,BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,M-DOWN> ... state LOWERLAYERDOWN

$ python3 firmware/mac_changer.py -i veth0 --live --set 01:00:5e:00:00:00
[+] Changing MAC on veth0
    Current: 96:A6:77:A3:EB:8C
    New:     01:00:5E:00:00:00
    Vendor:  Unknown
[-] Error: RTNETLINK answers: Cannot assign requested address

$ ip -o link show veth0
3: veth0@veth1: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,M-DOWN> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state DOWN \
       link/ether 96:a6:77:a3:eb:8c
```

Measured with an explicit flag check:

```
UP-flag present before failed change: 1
UP-flag present after  failed change: 0
```

The `UP` administrative flag is gone and `state` is `DOWN`. The same result was reproduced for `00:00:00:00:00:00` and `ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff`.

## Expected vs actual

| | |
|---|---|
| **Expected** | A failed MAC change leaves the interface exactly as it was found (up, original address). |
| **Actual** | The interface is left administratively **down** with the original address, and nothing in the tool reports that the link was dropped. |

This is the worst possible moment to discover the failure, because on a real host the interface is the one carrying the session that issued the command.

## Safe remediation plan

Lowest-risk first step, no behaviour change on the success path:

1. **Wrap the down/address/up sequence in `try/finally`** and bring the link back up in the `finally`, matching the state observed before the `down`:
   ```python
   was_up = self._is_up(interface)          # ip -o link show, parse ',UP,'
   subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface, 'down'], check=True, ...)
   try:
       subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface, 'address', new_mac],
                      check=True, ...)
   finally:
       subprocess.run(['ip', 'link', 'set', interface, 'up'], check=True, ...)
   ```
   If the `finally` raise needs suppressing, wrap it so the original error still propagates.
2. **Then** make the rollback state-aware (only re-`up` if the interface was up before), so an intentionally-down interface is not brought up behind the operator's back.
3. **Separately**, reject reserved addresses before touching the link at all — see the companion finding on `parse_mac` accepting kernel-rejected MACs. That removes the most common trigger but is *not* a substitute for the rollback, because `ip` can still fail for permission or driver reasons.

**Note on side effects:** step 1 changes the netlink sequence only on the failure path. The success path (`down` → `address` → `up`) is byte-for-byte the same, so no existing behaviour or test result changes.

items.title: Use invoking user's pattern directory when run under sudo
items.body:
Closes #55

## Problem
Under `sudo`, `user.Current()` returns root, so `getPatternDir()` resolved to `/root/.gf`. That directory usually doesn't exist, so every lookup failed with `no such pattern`.

## Change
- `getPatternDir()` now checks `~/.config/gf` and then `~/.gf` for the current user (same order as before).

- If nothing is found, it returns the same default as before (`~/.gf` of the current user), so `-save` behaviour is unchanged.
- README now mentions `~/.config/gf` and the sudo fallback.

## Verification
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go build` are clean. The repo has no tests.
- I simulated root with `unshare -r` (uid 0, home `/root`, which isn't accessible) and `SUDO_USER=$USER`:
  - old binary: `gf aws-keys` gave `no such pattern`
  - new binary: `gf -list` lists the user's patterns, and `gf aws-keys` matches as expected
  - running as a normal user works as before

## Assumptions
- If root has its own pattern directory, it still takes precedence over the sudo user's, so existing root setups don't change.

| `unshare -r touch /tmp/x` | ALLOW, targets=[] | BLOCK |
| `busybox patch /tmp/x` | ALLOW, targets=[] | BLOCK |

`unshare PROGRAM`, `nsenter … PROGRAM`, `chroot NEWROOT COMMAND` and `busybox APPLET` run the word
after the prefix, so those verdicts are the `builtin cd <outside>` hole (#1362) one prefix further
out, and the fix is the one that hole got: name the prefix. The semantics are util-linux's and
busybox's documented behaviour, **read rather than executed** — no `unshare`, `nsenter`, `chroot`
or `busybox` binary exists on the host this was measured on, and no row in the test executes
anything (pure predicates only).

## The fence issue #1513 needs

The named-wrapper branch of `_nested_command_texts` takes `tokens[i + 1:]` with no position test;
that is the only reason `unshare -r sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/x"` is read today. Measured, patching that
branch in-process to consult `_runs_as_a_command` before collecting the tail (the fix #1513
proposes, and the right one for the *mention* shapes it enumerates): the real-invocation shapes it
lists stay refused, but every payload behind a prefix that is **not** in `_COMMAND_WRAPPERS` opens
— and that set includes these four:

```
busybox sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/x"       BLOCK -> ALLOW
chroot / sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/x"      BLOCK -> ALLOW
unshare -r sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/x"    BLOCK -> ALLOW
nsenter -t 1 sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/x"  BLOCK -> ALLOW
```

With the four names present, the position test keeps reading them. `tests/test_exec_prefix_wrappers.py`
asserts that half, so the change that would open them has to look at the row.

## Tests

`tests/test_exec_prefix_wrappers.py`, three directions, pure predicates, nothing executed:

- the mutator behind each prefix is believed — `_find_git_mutator` for the git rows, a named target
  for the write rows;
- the shell-payload rows (`unshare -r sh -c …`, `chroot / /bin/sh -c …`, `busybox bash -c …`) stay
  read — the #1513 fence;
- the complement: reads behind the same prefixes (`busybox ls -l`, `unshare -r git status`,
  `nsenter -t 1 cat f.txt`, `unshare --map-root-user git status`) and quoted mentions stay ALLOW, so
  a change that refused everything would not pass either.

Local, on this branch: `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — **4443 passed, 214 skipped, 7 failed**, all 7
pre-existing on master and environmental for this host: 1×
`test_check_merge_order.py::TestAgainstRealGitHistory::test_the_shapes_git_really_prints` (this
host's git rejects `merge-tree --write-tree --quiet`, exit 129) and 6× `test_review_queue.py` (the
vote-window prose rows).

Contributor PR — measured at the read-only tier, no gatekeeping vote cast here.

items.title: fix(test): skip unwritable-parent fixture under root (cyril-uu8m)
items.body:
## Issue

cyril-uu8m — `host_io::tests::write_atomic_unwritable_parent_errs_target_intact` fails under euid 0 because root bypasses the 0o555 parent's permission bits (same bug class as cyril-jwi5 / PR #86).

## Route

**Local** — test-only guard inside one existing responsibility; the single system premise has valid current evidence (issue repro, PR #86 precedent, in-session red repro); no interface, ownership, or production change. Route record: `.cyril-uu8m/route.md`.

## Repro

`unshare -r env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR cargo nextest run -p cyril-core --features kas write_atomic_unwritable_parent` on unmodified `f9bc81d8` (`unshare -r` maps the caller to uid 0 in a user namespace; `unshare -r id -u` → `0`):

```
FAIL [   0.005s] (1/1) cyril-core protocol::kas::host_io::tests::write_atomic_unwritable_parent_errs_target_intact
thread '...' panicked at crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/kas/host_io.rs:495:43:
unwritable parent must fail the write: ()
Summary [   0.007s] 1 test run: 0 passed, 1 failed, 1072 skipped
```

Full receipt: `.cyril-uu8m/repro-red.log` (nextest exit 100).

## Cause

The fixture chmods the parent to `0o555` and expects `write_atomic` to fail at temp-file creation. With euid 0 the kernel ignores the permission bits (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE), the temp file is created, the rename succeeds, and `expect_err` panics. The permission-bit premise the test relies on simply does not hold for root; the production code is correct.

## Fix

Add the same `nix::unistd::geteuid().is_root()` early-return guard PR #86 gave `host_shell.rs::system_host_checks_effective_execute_permission` (`host_shell.rs:800-810`), mirroring its shape and its logged reason with the fixture name substituted:

```
skipping unwritable-parent fixture: euid is 0 and root bypasses permission bits
```

A visible `eprintln!` skip, never a silent pass. Non-root runs still execute the full fixture and all three assertions. 14 lines, all inside `#[cfg(test)]`; no production code changes; `nix` (`user` feature) was already a `cfg(unix)` dependency of cyril-core.

## Fence

Both receipts are committed under `.cyril-uu8m/` and were captured with `--success-output immediate` so a passing test's stderr is shown:

- **Root skip path** — `unshare -r env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR cargo nextest run -p cyril-core --features kas --success-output immediate write_atomic_unwritable_parent` → `PASS`, captured stderr is exactly the skip line above (`.cyril-uu8m/verify-root.log`).
- **Non-root assertion path** (`id -u` → 1000) — same command without `unshare -r` → `PASS`, **no** stderr section, `grep -c "skipping unwritable-parent"` = 0, so the fixture and assertions executed (`.cyril-uu8m/verify-nonroot.log`).

Red→green contrast on the same revision base: before the guard the root run fails at `host_io.rs:495`; after, it passes with the logged skip, and the non-root path is unchanged.

## Gate

Every command run with real exit codes (`cmd > log 2>&1 && echo GATE-OK-<name>`; a missing echo is a failure). Note: this shell exports `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=""`, which cargo rejects, so each command carries `env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (or the equivalent explicit worktree `target/` path) — no shared target dir.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | PASS |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | PASS — 2057 run, 2057 passed, 13 skipped |
| `cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features` | PASS — 2 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (default features) | PASS |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace` (default features) | PASS — 2055 run, 2055 passed, 13 skipped |
| `cargo clippy -p cyril -p cyril-core --features kas --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `cargo nextest run -p cyril -p cyril-core --features kas` | PASS — 1250 run, 1250 passed, 10 skipped |
| `cargo clippy -p cyril-core --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` (CI mirror, extra) | PASS |
| `cargo nextest run -p cyril-core --no-default-features` (CI mirror, extra) | PASS — 782 run, 782 passed, 4 skipped |

## Discovered, not fixed

- The guard keys on `geteuid() == 0` as a proxy for CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, exactly like PR #86. A non-root process holding that capability would still see the fixture "fail" (write succeeds); that configuration is not one CI or `unshare -r` produces, and widening the guard to a capability probe was out of the approved scope.
- Tool-shell environment: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is exported as an empty string in the agent shell, which makes every bare `cargo` invocation fail before building. Worked around per-command; not a repository issue.

`poldek --noconf` with no `-O` option leaves `ctx->htconf` NULL, and the

items.title: safety: the deployment installs the notify unit, and enables nothing
items.body:
`bin/domum-media` is the only executable that changed — but the weekly unit carries the `health-notify` `ExecStart`, so **installing the file is what makes the notification available**, and the deployment did not touch units at all. Without this, turning the feature on needed a second, unrehearsed step.

It now installs `/etc/systemd/system/domum-media-weekly-report.{service,timer}` at **0644** when their hashes differ, runs `daemon-reload`, and **enables nothing**. The report prints the `systemctl enable --now` line, so starting to send mail stays an explicit operator decision.

## Rehearsal additions

- the unit is installed **0644** and matches the checkout byte-for-byte;
- the **reload really happened** — asserted against a recording `systemctl` stub, not assumed;
- **no `enable`/`start`/`restart`** was ever issued, asserted against *both* the script's own text and the calls it made;
- an **unchanged** unit is not reinstalled on a second run.

## A sandbox may provide a dependency; it may not weaken the check

systemd is unreachable inside `unshare -r`, so a real `daemon-reload` fails and the deployment aborts — **correctly**, because a failed reload means systemd has not seen the new unit. The rehearsal supplies a recording `systemctl` stub on `PATH`, exactly as it already supplies a fake git upstream, and then asserts the call.

Making the reload non-fatal to suit the test would have been the wrong fix.

items.title: Chromium keeps renderer shared memory in /dev/shm, not /tmp (PL-157)
items.body:
PL-157. Playwright launches Chromium with `--disable-dev-shm-usage`, which puts the renderer's shared memory in `/tmp`. On sartre `/tmp` is a quota-limited tmpfs; when the quota fills, renderers crash and `pnpm e2e` fails at random (`Page crashed`, `Target crashed`).

- `web/playwright.config.ts`: the `chromium` project launches with `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--disable-dev-shm-usage']`, so shared memory goes to `/dev/shm`.
- verify-punchlist (`SKILL.md`, `features/web-app.md`, `features/projects.md`): Chromium launched by hand in a check uses the same option.

## Live checks

Each run used a private 2 GB tmpfs on `/tmp` (`unshare -r --mount`), filled to 200 MB free, so the checks did not fill the `/tmp` that other agents share. The full report and scripts are attached to PL-157.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/tmp` 200 MB free, `pnpm e2e` ×3, main vs branch | No crash messages or core dumps on either side. Main's Chromium drove the private `/tmp` to 0 MB free and the branch's never went below 197 MB, but main did not crash, so the crash did not reproduce. Both sides fail only `projects.spec.ts:118` in every run: a pre-existing failure on main (PL-161). |
| 2 | Shared memory in `/dev/shm` | Pass. `/proc/<pid>/maps`: main maps up to 68 `/tmp/.org.chromium.*` files and 0 from `/dev/shm`; the branch maps 0 from `/tmp` and up to 70 from `/dev/shm`. |
| 3 | `/tmp` empty, timing | Pass. Median wall time is 26.2 s on main and 26.1 s on the branch (3 alternating pairs). `issues.spec.ts:617` is flaky on both: 3/15 on main, 1/15 on the branch (PL-162). |
| 4 | verify-punchlist screen check, `/tmp` filled | Pass. The screenshot was taken. |

items.title: M6-05 part 1: workspace seccomp = runner's profile + ptrace
items.body:
M6-05, **part 1 only** (seccomp convergence, 06 §6.2). The rest of the card (resize, cgroup slices, host nft, Caddy log mask, backups, `deployment.md` §3) is still to do.

## What changes

`apps/codespace/infra/seccomp/codespace.json` was containers-common's default plus `personality(ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE)`. It is now `apps/runner/infra/seccomp/runner.json` plus **one** rule allowing `ptrace` (gdb), placed right after the main allow list.

No longer allowed in the workspace:
- `unshare`, `setns` (it keeps its `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` rule, which never applies under `--cap-drop=ALL`)
- `mount`, `umount`, `umount2`, `pivot_root`
- the new mount API: `fsopen`, `fsmount`, `fsconfig`, `fspick`, `move_mount`, `open_tree`, `mount_setattr`
- `keyctl`, `name_to_handle_at`
- `clone` with a `CLONE_NEW*` flag (mask `0x7E020000`); `clone3` now answers `ENOSYS`

Nothing else needed adding. `personality` and `process_vm_readv` were already in the runner's profile.

## One source of truth

`apps/codespace/src/engine/seccomp.test.ts` (unit suite, runs in CI) removes the `ptrace` rule and deep-compares the rest with the runner's file. It also checks that no namespace or mount syscall is allowed without a condition. The file stays committed rather than generated because the deploy installs it as it is (`deploy/lib.sh`). With the test, any drift turns CI red instead of becoming an extra deploy step.

## Image test

`images/c-dev/test.sh` § 10 checks five things:
- `unshare -r true` and `unshare -U true` fail with ENOSYS
- `mount -t tmpfs` fails
- the raw `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` and `mount(2)` calls answer ENOSYS
- gdb `-batch -ex 'break main' -ex run -ex next -ex step -ex bt` stops in `main`, steps into `square (x=3)`, and its backtrace shows `main` below it

## Tests run

- `pnpm --filter @quiz/codespace test`: 22 files, 263 tests pass. `typecheck` is clean.
- `APPARMOR= images/c-dev/test.sh` on the WSL2 workstation (rootful socket, `--remote`): all 51 assertions pass. That covers code-server `/healthz`, git, and § 10.
- The same probes under the **previous** profile: `unshare -r true` **succeeded** and `mount(2)` answered `EPERM`.
- Also checked under the new profile: clangd `--check`, a pty (`script`), git gc, Node worker threads.
- Not checked: the extension host and the terminal in a real browser session.

## Deploy note

The next codespace deploy installs the new profile. A session container keeps the filter it was created with until it is created again. The AppArmor profile is unchanged. No server was touched by this PR.
